## Alpha 0.1 shared app design — 2026-10-17

The approved Model Studio presentation now lives in shared Aether UI and is
adopted by all eight frontends in the existing GitHub repositories. Transparent
headers, compact settings/app/account controls, matched resizable floating cards,
separate auxiliary panels, contextual tools and right-aligned file tray actions
preserve each application's real operations. Saved layouts and theme preferences
are respected. CAD/Map/Sketch/IO use bottom tools; Animation retains a top tool
tray where its timeline needs the space. Vector adopts the home and navigation
foundation; its editor remains unimplemented.

UI145/assets27 and product-specific session peer updates are pinned as versioned
archives. Session runtime files are unchanged. Model Studio neutral colors,
rendering/environment presets, feature-tree controls and artwork remain shared.
Public Alpha 0.1 preparation uses isolated source snapshots and checksum-locked
release attachments. No native installation cutover or desktop installer is
implied. `ALPHA_0_1.md` records the concrete limits in each product; evidence is in
`.verification/alpha-0.1-2026-10-17/`. The public Alpha release carries its qualification and source manifests.

## CAD saved-file programs and exact verification — 2026-10-13 (development)

CAD's saved-file catalog now has 14 source commands. New `cad.part.docs`,
`cad.part.runprogram` and `cad.part.verify` expose discovery, bounded modeling
programs and exact physical-property proof through the native host and CLI/MCP.
The eight supported step types reuse the open editor's preparation/reference
logic. Each step rebuilds in FreeCAD and resolves real body identities; only the
completed candidate returns for one guarded Studio save. Later-step failure,
stale revision or denied permission does not persist a partial edit. No-op
programs add no revision; identical operation-ID retries reuse the receipt.

tests with real FreeCAD; 8 native Rust host tests against private disposable
PostgreSQL, including actual MCP program execution and CLI receipt replay.

fixture builds an 80×50×10 mm plate with radius-5 mm through bore, verifies
`40000 - 250π` mm³ and density-based mass, then reopens the saved document.
Evidence: `../Aether-CAD/.verification/classcad-headless-2026-10-13/`.
Qualified native worker SHA256:
`235f22830657bd140ee8f536ff73f8fe914084872710048008d36d1c7ee4633b`.

### CAD sketch-to-extrude and interactive depth — 2026-10-12

Replaced the 2.5-second DOM polling handoff with explicit asynchronous sketch
completion. Repeated solid-tool clicks do not enqueue duplicate dialogs; failure
keeps the sketch open with its error; success retains the requested operation.
Finishing a sketch passes its selected region, or its sole closed region, into
the next Extrude editor. Ambiguous multi-region sketches still require selection.

Extrude has an on-model depth handle using the viewer's evaluated sketch frame
and ray/axis projection, including perspective and orthographic cameras. Dragging
changes the real parameter through the existing native preview/commit path;
crossing the sketch plane reverses direction. Escape/pointer cancellation restores
the starting values. The handle supports a single sketch source with a blind end,
zero starting offset and no second end. It hides when the axis is effectively
end-on; the feature panel retains numeric input plus drag depth/keyboard controls.
Symmetric and more complex extents retain their parameter controls. The UI does
not implement arbitrary face movement or direct face push/pull.

Preview requests are coalesced at 100 ms during continuous edits, retain the last
valid model while awaiting its replacement, and reject stale results. Invalid
parameters and cancellation clear previews. This improves interaction continuity
without changing or faking native geometry.

## Authorized document change stream — 2026-10-11

The native Rust host now exposes a same-origin, authenticated SSE endpoint for
read-only document invalidation. It reports committed Main/branch revisions,
branch metadata, named versions, discussions and current edit permission. Every
reconnect rechecks durable state, so a missed metadata change is recovered even
without a process-local event buffer. Intermediate changes may coalesce; this is
current-state delivery, not operation replay or concurrent editing.

Access is rechecked on each poll under the current identity/access locks. Session
or document revocation and disabled apps close the stream without new document
state. Defaults bound subscriptions at 512 and concurrent snapshot reads at 4;
checks retain no idle database connection or application producer queue. Watching
never changes documents, enrollment, recent-file entries or revision history.

The browser editors do not consume this endpoint yet. Safe browser invalidation,
reconnect/edit conflict behavior, company workload qualification and the remaining
app/admin/agent/offline/cutover gates remain open. No frontend package release,
database schema change, production restart or push occurred.

Standalone tear-off removes the source tab and uses a separate session tab list; project element tabs remain because they represent project contents. Popup rejection/save errors are surfaced; unsaved drafts cannot detach. This is browser-window support, not native Safari tab integration; embedded-browser OS-window behavior remains unverified.

Native part/project tab switching now reuses the worker/viewer and mounted shell instead of location.assign. Current edits flush before transport identity changes; competing switches are rejected and input is temporarily inert during loading. Active sketch/feature editing must finish/cancel first. Navigation failures retain the prior URL/session identity and restore the previous saved view after partial engine failures; Back/Forward uses the same loader. Old assembly projection is closed when returning to a part. Tree/inspector content necessarily follows the current document. Direct STEP import remains the legacy importer; per-tab undo/camera retention and cross-window redocking are not implemented.

## CAD independent parity: Extrude Intersect — 2026-10-09

In the new `aether-cad` repository, Extrude now enables Intersect for a single
existing target. It retains only the volume shared by the extrusion and target,
preserves the target identity, and leaves other bodies unchanged. It uses the
native FreeCAD region path, with supported depth/symmetric/offset/opposite-depth
and through-all controls. Missing targets and empty overlap produce diagnostics;
failed builds cannot be exported. Revolve/Sweep Intersect remain disabled.

Existing document persistence accepts `intersect`; the parked browser evaluator
refuses it explicitly. Older readers without the operation reject these features;
this does not claim backwards execution compatibility or a new fallback kernel.
Native coverage includes analytical volumes, suppression, depth edits, invalid
input recovery and STEP export/reimport. The mounted authoring flow verifies
selection/target requirements and serialization. A real browser on disposable
host9478 selected a sketch face, previewed/committed Intersect, edited 6 to 8 mm,
reloaded the hosted document and canceled a later through-all preview. The saved
revision 3 retained Intersect, 8 mm, the original generated body identity and
Blind. No production data was changed.

Verification: 874 app tests (native integrations enabled), 148 native tests
with FreeCAD required, seven installed-service tests with native gate enabled;
legacy-engine regression and type/build checks. Scoped new-test/regions lint and
all 12 repository boundaries pass. Worker/extent lint has 14 pre-existing findings,
verified unchanged against HEAD; this slice does not claim those files lint clean.
Full Onshape parity remains open. See
[the independent parity inventory](../roadmap/Aether_CAD_Onshape_Parity.md).

## Map/CAD framework compatibility and release gates — 2026-10-09

New repositories now ship platform API 1 compatibility declarations inside the
Map 0.2.0a4 and CAD 0.2.0a3 service wheels; both require platform 0.2.0a3.
The host rejects incompatible declared identities/APIs before service construction.

hashes and installed shared package versions. Static architecture guards now catch
CAD-engine imports outside CAD (apart from the existing UI gallery reference),
shared UI transport/product imports, sketch renderer/UI imports, URL/glob source
crossings, and ordinary cross-repository imports. All 12 repository roots pass.

`suite.py release --workers 2` builds shared packages, Studio, Map and CAD before
running focused acceptance. It requires the native CAD document workflows as well
as engine and installed-wheel tests; skipped or empty native runs fail. Reports
record source/change fingerprints, archive hashes, output hashes, commands, timing
and logs. Failed preflight cannot reuse an old successful report. This is local
verification, not an installer or deployment operation.

Map621, CAD871 (all eight previously optional native integration tests enabled),

in this work, and no production data or physical device was touched.

## Map product agent adapter — 2026-10-09 (new repositories)

Map agents can inspect saved scenes/surfaces/timelines/tracks/assets, evaluate a
scene's Main composition at a time, and move/duplicate/delete/split/trim clips.

compositor. `normalizeDocument` is also used by editor opening/reset/edit paths.

locks, incompatible tracks and stale revisions refuse edits. Content edits save
ordinary recoverable history; open editors reload and keep existing conflict checks.
Map's wheel includes its bundled runtime and requires platform 0.2.0a2; both service
packages are now 0.2.0a2. Node.js is required on the host. Suite tests include the new
Map service tests.

## Raspberry Pi appliance and temporary live mirroring — 2026-10-08

Show → Players retains independent deployment and adds Mirror live / Stop
mirroring for paired online devices. The browser shares a chosen output window
or tab over LAN WebRTC; owner-authenticated, token-bound offers/answers expire
without a sender heartbeat. The Pi's Python daemon proxies signalling for its
loopback kiosk without exposing the device token to JavaScript. The persistent
kiosk shell can receive a cast before deployment, unloads the saved renderer
while live video plays (avoiding competing audio), and restarts the assigned
show with its existing schedule after explicit stop, sender loss or signalling
failure. The saved show assignment is never changed by casting. Live capture
requires a supporting browser on HTTPS/localhost and LAN peer connectivity;
audio capture depends on the selected source/browser. No external TURN service.

The downloadable installer now bundles player/setup/receiver; skips apt when
prerequisites exist; preserves a configured host on reinstall; enables desktop
autologin; starts the dedicated-profile Chromium kiosk from labwc/XDG with the
graphical environment; waits for its local daemon; grants scoped NetworkManager
operations. Wi-Fi profiles autoconnect with retry. First-run setup offers a
per-device password and fixed 192.168.4.1:8777 address, is reachable from the LAN,
and closes remotely after setup. Device files use restrictive permissions and
atomic config replacement. Device mute applies to served master audio without
changing stored show bytes; renderer-freeze permission preserves an installed
bundle. Setup/pair/rename dialogs now portal above inspectors and use compact
width, fixing the obstructed Done action observed during acceptance.

Verification: Map602 tests, production build, lint (existing warnings), repository
guards; 87 Python player/setup/provisioning/device/cast checks and three final
Chrome/Python flows on9354 covering setup + deploy/offline/mirror/fallback/stop. Actual
WebRTC peers receive changing canvas frames (only the sharing picker is faked).
Physical Pi installation/reboot, Wi-Fi AP handover, HDMI audio, sustained GPU
performance and cold-boot clock accuracy remain unverified. Requires Pi OS
Desktop; this download is an installer, not an SD-card image. Schedules use the
Pi's local clock/time zone; existing Main loop/hold and daily/weekday rules remain.

## Map reusable timelines in Media Pool — 2026-10-06

## Reusable Media Pool sources and visual timeline tracks — 2026-10-05

Map format 5 separates reusable Media Pool source records from scheduled visual
clips. Clips reference a source and can explicitly override its source settings;
timing, opacity, effects and targets remain instance-owned. Legacy format 1–4
content migrates while preserving clip identity, timing, ordering and geometry.
Source references round-trip; broken/missing pool identities reject loading
instead of silently dropping clips. Pool entries survive deletion of their uses;
in-use source deletion is blocked. Referenced media remain protected from cleanup.

Visualization has an upper-left Media Pool with thumbnails/list, search, bins,
Import, Generators and Effects. Generators add reusable shader/text sources;
Effects applies an existing supported effect to the selected clip. Selecting a
pool item previews its source and opens source properties. Dragging into a track
creates a distinct clip at the drop time; Append adds it after that track's last
clip. The former Assets tree is labeled Clip index and lists scheduled uses.

The timeline has scene and surface tabs, named visual tracks, track hide/lock and
ordering, and multiple sequential clips per track. Extra tracks layer content.
Track order is used by both canvas and projector output; legacy reorder commands
remain connected. Independent duplication makes a new track, and editing clip
timing does not accidentally convert inherited source settings into overrides.

Scope: the Scene tab is an all-track overview, **not a nested master timeline**.
Jonathan's compound timeline proposal is recorded in the acceptance roadmap:
logical surface groups with their own tracks and one scheduled master layer.
Compound-instance scheduling, audio soundtrack tracks, clip-local spatial
composition controls and full Lazy Lighting/Resolve parity are not implemented
by this work. Existing multi-target Repeat/Span clips continue to work.

## Map Assets tree controls visual stacking — 2026-10-04

## Selecting a file: commands on top, details beside — 2026-10-04

Picking a file in Drive or an app home now puts its commands in the row above

rather than staying a 180px column.

## Audio-aware visualization quick setup — 2026-10-04

Shader Properties now includes Audio response quick setup: Beat pulse, Bass
pulse, Treble shimmer, Full mix and manual Tempo pulse (30–240 BPM). These write
ordinary scale/rotation modulation assignments, keeping existing unrelated
assignments and the detailed per-parameter editor authoritative. All 29 current
shader presets support the quick audio assignments. No new visual catalog or

period plus clock=scene so local visual loops do not reset it. Optional
audioSignal=beat selects the transient signal; legacy audio bindings are unchanged.

editor input without requesting a second microphone. Deployed/offline players
still require their own live-audio implementation; no remote audio capture is claimed.

## Dialogs keep the caret where you put it — 2026-10-03

Typing a name into any dialog in the suite moved focus out of the field after
every single letter, so a name had to be entered one click per character. The
cause was in the shared dialog: its focus-management ran again on every render,
handing focus back to whatever opened the dialog and then to the first element
inside it, which is the close button in the title bar. It now runs once when the
dialog opens, and it focuses the field the content asked for rather than the
close button. Every dialog in every app is fixed by this, not just the new-file
one.

the folder it went to. Creating has never opened the editor and still does not.

## Always-on hosted document services — 2026-10-03

Map, CAD, IO, Sketch and hosted Animation now connect the standard sidebar to the
Studio library: autosave history, named versions, branches, compare, restore,
whole-file merge, file sharing, threaded comments, document notes, tasks and
reminders. Studio's history/collaboration dialog uses the same Aether UI panels.
CAD's revision-management opt-out no longer disables history. Product edit
serializers remain product-owned; shared session adapters manage save sequencing,
branch head checks and recovery. Branch editing and restoration append history;
versions retain immutable revision references. A selected historical revision
is read-only. Copy recovery creates a different document rather than overwriting
the source, and switching IO documents isolates their autosave queues.

Collaboration records have their own revision and append-only change journal,
independent of document autosaves. Authentication, library permissions and
workspace membership guard access; authors/owners and assigned-task roles govern
mutations. Conflicting notes/item drafts remain available for review. Existing
CAD device-local reminders remain accessible separately when present.

This is not full Git/Onshape/Microsoft 365 parity: merges resolve entire file
snapshots, polling refreshes collaboration, and reminders have in-app due/status
tracking without email/push delivery. External/local animation files still use
the engine-file workflow; hosted library files receive the suite services.

Verification: host suite passed (154 tests at that checkpoint), then 23 focused
host cases including stale merge-source guards; all seven web builds; shared UI
and product checks; Chrome flows across all five authoring apps for version,
comments, tasks, notes and refresh, Map branch compare/restore, CAD and Animation
autosave, Sketch conflict-copy recovery and IO document-switch isolation. The
running shared Studio host was not restarted; it must reload the Python modules
to expose the new backend endpoints. Fresh isolated test hosts use the new code.

## A version is a named version — 2026-10-03

The version chip in the file manager counts named versions, not saves. A
document that has been edited all afternoon but never versioned shows no chip
at all, where it used to show a number in the dozens taken from the autosave
counter. Hovering a chip names the version behind it. Rows read icon, name and
type — Part Studio, Assembly, Project or Drawing — with the date dropped.

The save counter still travels with every file and still guards concurrent
edits; it is simply not what the chip means.

Verified: 155 host tests, 381 Aether UI; CAD build.

## Part manager is a file manager — 2026-10-03

the way Onshape lists a document's tabs. Below them the library browses by
folder with a path to walk back, each document carrying its version, the way
Fusion shows a directory. One search filters both at once, a folder opens in
place rather than as a document, and with nothing open the panel is the library
alone.

It is a shared widget rather than an Aether CAD panel, so the other apps can
show the same file manager over their own stores.

## Version control merges, compares, and manages branches — 2026-10-02

Aether Studio's document history now does what git and Onshape do. A branch can
be merged into another: when only the branch moved the merge goes straight
through, and when both sides moved the host reports what differs and asks which
side wins, recording the merge with both parents either way. Any two revisions
can be compared, with native CAD parts reporting which features were added,
removed and changed. Branches can be renamed and deleted, with deletion refusing
to discard unmerged work unless told to. Versions can be renamed, described and
deleted. Restoring while working in a branch now moves that branch; it used to
rewrite Main.

Aether CAD's Versions and history panel reaches all of it, and its marks are now
drawn as Onshape draws them.

## Versions and history looks and works like the reference — 2026-10-02

Aether CAD's version panel now follows Onshape's: a titled header whose actions
are icons, a search field, Name and Modified columns, one tree down the left
with an icon marking each row's kind, a legend explaining every mark, and the
right-click hint. Each version folds the saves made after it under a disclosure
of its own. Clicking a row selects it, and Restore makes that revision the
current state again; the previous state stays in history.

The host's version model is git-shaped: content-addressed storage, a chain of
revisions, named versions, branches from any revision, read-only checkout of
any revision, and restore. Merge and compare are drawn but disabled, each with
a tooltip saying why; merge waits on the engine.

## Aether UI moves, and works under a finger — 2026-09-30

Motion is now part of a theme: three durations and three easing curves that every
transition in the design system spends, so a theme can slow the interface down or
flatten it. Turning on reduced motion stills the whole suite, including the busy
indicator and the spinner, which previously ignored it. Menus, popovers,
tooltips, the command palette, toasts and dialogs fade and settle in rather than
appearing at full strength; tabs, disclosure chevrons, the bottom panel and the
split pane move rather than jump.

A theme also carries touch geometry. On a coarse pointer, rows, rails, controls
and control padding grow to the 44px a finger needs, and the drag handles that
were 4 to 15 pixels grow their grab area so the gestures that already existed can
actually be reached.

Two things were broken on a tablet and are fixed. A side panel opened from the
rail never appeared, because the narrow layout hid it until a hover that touch
cannot produce. A dialog with a long body ran off the screen with nothing to
scroll. The split pane no longer caps its primary pane so wide that the other
side is unusable, and the dashboard's narrow layout now triggers above tablet
portrait width rather than 20px below it.

Verified: 324 Aether UI tests, typecheck, build, and the theme-literal and
icon-pack guards.

## Map device deployment is authorized, not just checked — 2026-09-29

Deploying a show to a projector now reads the library as the person doing it.
Assignment previously accepted any Map document that existed, so a signed-in
person could push a stranger's private show to their own device; it now requires
that they own the show or that it is shared with the workspace, the same rule the
library applies everywhere else. The projector re-checks that rule on every pull
rather than trusting the deploy: when a show stops being shared, the next pull
returns no show and the device goes dark instead of continuing to project what it
cached.

Not yet true: a device announcing itself still receives its show token, and its
pairing code, without proving it is that device — knowing the public device id is
enough. Closing it requires a device-held secret and therefore an updated player
on every existing Pi, so it waits on a deployment decision. Device media reads
are also still not scoped to the assigned document, though media names are
random enough that the store is a capability space rather than a listing.

Verified: 123 core/host tests, ruff clean. Both new tests confirmed to fail with
the fix reverted.

## Map point rounding, reflection and precision controls — 2026-09-28

Mapping's Properties panel now supports horizontal/vertical reflection of an
individual surface or whole compound, including every mask profile, around one
selection pivot. All faces change in one Undo transaction; any locked member
blocks the operation. Group selection displays the group name and count instead
of the unrelated Output / Nothing selected inspector.

In Node mode, selecting a square mask handle exposes Round amount and Round
selected point. The operation trims the adjacent edges and creates a sampled
tangent quadratic curve in the existing polygon format; Undo restores the corner.

share exactly the same clipping points, without a format migration.

bypasses snapping; no persistent weld is implied. Mapping precision in Properties
controls snap enable/distance, node-pin size and canvas grid visibility. Those
screen-space preferences persist in browser storage and do not alter projection
or document geometry. Existing bounds/center snapping uses the same tolerance.

## Aether Animation on the shared chrome and stage; one viewport reader for every product — 2026-09-29

**Aether Animation** was the only product whose header carried no appearance
or theme control; it now has both, grouped with its layout button the way CAD
and Map do. Its 3D viewport painted a hardcoded background, grid, part and
selection colour, so no theme reached it. It reads the theme's `viewport-*`
tokens now and repaints when the theme changes, keeping its own colours only
as fallbacks. The axis triad stays red, green and blue, which is a convention
rather than a theme choice.

**One reader, shared.** The token-to-number reader written for Aether CAD
moved into the library as `core/ui/src/viewport-theme.ts`
(`readViewportPalette`), since it is presentation and nothing else: it parses
the theme's colour forms and hands back numbers a renderer can use, including
the single background colour a solid scene needs, which is the stage
gradient's midpoint. CAD's module is now a thin adapter that shapes the
palette for its appearance resolver, and Animation reads the palette directly.
A test checks every interface theme resolves a complete stage and that a
viewport theme may restyle only part of one.

**A defect of mine, found and fixed.** `setAetherTheme` and
`setAetherViewportTheme` dispatched their change event without checking for a
document, so calling either outside a browser threw. Both are guarded now, and
the library's theme test covers choosing an interface theme and a viewport
theme independently.

**Aether CAD's Background setting** is pinned by a test: every render
environment it ships has a viewport theme of the same name, and "slate", which
it used to offer and which was never a valid preset, is gone.

Verified: 301 library tests, 455 Map, 774 CAD with the same 4 failures that
pre-date this work, five product builds, both guards. Still open across the
suite: CAD, Map and Animation each compose their own toolbar from ribbon
primitives instead of `WorkspaceRibbon`, which is the parked consolidation and
the last thing keeping the redesigned tool bar out of the products.

## Aether UI: the workspace switcher is a shared widget — 2026-09-22

Map had a hand-rolled workspace dropdown: a `MenuButton` plus local CSS in
`MapRibbon.css`. Jonathan, 2026-09-22: *"I do not like us generally have custom
local UI elements since I might want to reuse it in other apps."* Correct — and
the fix is the same shape as `TreePanel`, where the library owns the widget and
an application only supplies content.

**`WorkspaceSwitcher`** is now in `@aether/ui`: a button naming the room you are
in, with a menu of the rooms available. It owns its appearance, so no
application needs override CSS — which is the point. It names itself
`Workspace: Mapping` rather than "Workspace", because an app may also have a
workspace *window* menu and two controls with one name are ambiguous to anyone
reading by label.

Its stylesheet uses `button.aui-workspace-switcher`, element-plus-class,
deliberately. `.aui-menu-trigger` is an `inline-grid` with `border: 0`; a bare
class would tie with it and be decided by source order alone. That is exactly
how Map's local version failed — the caret stacked under the label and the box
vanished — and it is a trap for anyone styling a library component from an app.

**`WorkspaceRibbon` gained `workspaceLayout`**, so the library now offers both
arrangements rather than one: `"strip"` (the default, unchanged — workspaces as
tabs inside the tab row) and `"column"` (the switcher in a column of its own at
the far left, spanning both rows, with the tool tabs above the tools to its
right). The column is Fusion's arrangement and the more honest one: a workspace
is not a peer of the tool tabs, because choosing one changes which tool tabs
exist.

Map consumes the widget and its local appearance rules are gone; only the
placement of the column stays in `MapRibbon.css`, which is Map's business.
`WorkspaceRibbon` itself still has no application consumer — Map keeps its own
ribbon body because it has tool-variant menus and per-room tab memory the
library ribbon does not model. Converging those is the remaining work.

Verified: `core/ui` 209 tests passing, typecheck clean, build green;
`aether-map` 407 tests passing, build green, lint clean, and the ribbon, scenes
and artboards browser specs 14/14.

## Map: the workspace switcher is a button again, not a tab — 2026-09-22

Mapping and Sequence were drawn as tabs beside Create, Media and Output, which
read as a peer of them. They are not: a workspace is the room you are in, and
picking one changes which of the other tabs exist. It is a dropdown button
naming the current room again, ahead of the tab strip, which is what it was
before.

Placed the way Fusion places `DESIGN ▾`: a boxed control in a **column of its
own at the far left**, spanning the whole ribbon and centred against both rows,
with the tool tabs above the tools to its right. It is not a tab and does not
sit in the strip with them — picking it changes which tabs exist. This reverses
the earlier "the strip is the switcher" arrangement, whose reasoning is still
recorded at the top of `MapRibbon.css` so the trade is visible if anyone
revisits it. Getting there needed a specificity fix — `.aui-menu-trigger`
is an `inline-grid` with `border: 0`, and being a single class loaded after
`MapRibbon.css` it beat a single-class rule of ours, which stacked the caret
under the label and removed the box. Scoping to
`.map-ribbon-workspaces .map-workspace-button` settles it.

The control is labelled `Workspace: Mapping` rather than "Workspace" — the
document header already has a workspace *window* menu, and two controls sharing
one name is ambiguous to anyone reading by label. `switchWorkspace` in
`e2e/helpers.ts` drives the menu now, so every spec that changes rooms follows.

## Map: Cube and Box groups resize and rotate as one object — 2026-09-22

Selecting a Cube or Box folder now shows the standard eight corner/side resize
handles plus the rotation handle around the compound's full bounds. Dragging a
handle transforms every face through one shared group frame, so coincident
vertices and joined edges remain connected. Side handles adjust one axis,

controls, so face alignment remains available separately from solid sizing.

## Map: output-region boxes stay on their linked scene — 2026-09-22

The external output window already rendered the scene named by its output's
`sceneId`, but the editor's blue crop box was mounted inside whichever artboard
was active. Clicking Scene 2 therefore made an Output 1 box assigned to Scene 1
appear to jump onto Scene 2 even though the projector remained correct.

The region overlay now belongs to the same scene as the output. It stays
visible on that linked artboard while another scene is active, remains inert
there so controls cannot edit through an inactive artboard, and regains its
move/resize controls when its scene becomes active. Explicitly changing the
output's scene moves the box to the new artboard; merely selecting a scene does
not. Both active and inactive artboards carry stable scene identifiers for this
binding and for regression inspection.

Verified: 405 Map unit/component tests, production TypeScript/Vite build, lint
with the existing warnings, and the real-Chrome two-scene artboard workflow.
The browser test switches active scenes and output assignment independently,
checking the box remains on the output's linked artboard at every step.

## Map: repeated edits no longer exhaust Safari browser history — 2026-09-22

Autosave state notifications previously called `history.replaceState()` with
the same saved-document URL after every edit. Safari permits only 100 History
API calls in ten seconds, so ordinary shape work could trip a `SecurityError`
and open Map's recovery screen even though the document and autosave data were
still intact. URL replacement now has one shared equality boundary: the editor
writes once when it creates a draft and once when that draft gains a saved
document identity. Content edits, pending/saving/saved notifications and
repeated output-session messages do not rewrite an unchanged URL. Browser
history state and URL fragments are retained when an identity really changes.
The guard is local to each browsing context; recovery remains isolated by user
and document, and server saves retain their revision checks for simultaneous
users and projects.

Verified: 404 Map unit/component tests, production TypeScript/Vite build, lint
with the existing warnings, and the real-Chrome repeated-drag/property-edit
flow. That flow now installs a three-call History API limiter, completes all
edits without reaching it, and observes at most two URL writes.

## Map: surfaces may exist outside every scene artboard — 2026-09-21

Surface identity and scene assignment are now separate document facts. A
surface still owns its stable ID, geometry, assets, cues and group identity,
while its owner is either one scene or the workspace root. Dragging a surface
or selected Cube/Box off every artboard unlinks it from its scene, converts its
geometry into workspace coordinates and moves its row out from beneath the
scene in Layers. The root object remains visible and fully selectable with the
same body, resize, rotate, node, keyboard, Properties, asset and delete paths.
It is deliberately absent from every projector output. Dropping it onto an
artboard converts the geometry back to that scene's local coordinates, nests
the row under that scene, activates the scene and keeps the selection.

`.aethermap` version 3 now persists `unassignedSurfaces`; older files default
to an empty root collection. Autosave/Undo operate on the ownership transfer as
part of the pointer gesture. Media used only by an unassigned surface remains
referenced and cannot be cleaned up as an orphan.

Verified: 397 Map unit/component tests, production TypeScript/Vite build, lint
with the existing warnings, diff/whitespace, and all seven real-Chrome scene
workflows. Browser coverage unlinks a selected surface into the inter-artboard
workspace, confirms its root tree row, handles and dark output, then assigns it
to Scene 2 and confirms the nested row, selection and active render. Unit
coverage includes file round trips, single-surface ownership, scene output
exclusion, media retention and Cube group unlink/reassignment.

## Map: the Assets tab browses for content instead of listing it — 2026-09-21

The Assets tab answered "what did I import" but never "what could I import", so
finding something to project meant leaving the app. It is now two halves:
**Browse**, which searches openly-licensed content and imports it, and **In this
show**, which is what the tab used to be.

**Openverse is the first provider**, chosen because it needs no API key — the
tab works on a fresh install with nothing configured. Search is proxied by the
Studio host at `/api/map/assets/search`. Importing **downloads** the file into
the show's media store through the same path a local upload takes: a show runs
in a venue, often on a paired Pi, often with no network, and an asset left as a
URL is a black surface on the night. `MediaRef.credit` carries provider,
creator, licence and source URL into the document, because most open licences
require credit and a show that travels without its attribution cannot legally
be projected. Creator and licence are on each tile, not behind it — that is the
thing an operator has to know before it goes on a wall.

Two findings worth recording. Openverse answers **401** when `page_size`
exceeds 20 anonymously — an auth status for a paging problem, which reads as a
credentials failure and is not; the proxy now passes the upstream's own
`detail` text through rather than swallowing it. And the same search that
succeeds from a server is refused from a page, so proxying is not optional even
for a keyless provider.

**Sources that cannot be searched from here are cards**, folded under "More
places to find content": eleven of them, each with what it costs on its face and
a coloured edge — green free, amber mixed, grey paid — because cost is the first
thing you want and the last thing you should have to hunt for. Free and
projection-specific come first (4mapper, Lumabox, StageLoops), then free general
(Pixabay, Pexels, Openverse), then paid (VJ Loops Farm, Video Mapping Store,
Storyblocks, Motion Array, Pond5). The three with real APIs are marked
"integrable", which is also the shortlist for what to build next.

Worth knowing: **4mapper's video library is Pixabay content**, curated for
projection work — royalty-free, no attribution. Integrating the Pixabay API
would therefore bring those VJ loops, particles and smoke clips in natively,
which makes Pixabay the highest-value provider to add next.

URLs are canonical. Several arrived carrying Google Ads click ids and campaign
parameters; those are stripped, because shipping one would route operators
through someone else's ad attribution and would rot the moment the id expired.
A test asserts none come back. Nothing claims a licence — terms differ per site
and per clip, and the cards say so.

Planned, not built: `dev/docs/roadmap/Aether_Map_Asset_Providers.md` names the
provider interface, the manifest shape a third-party plugin would take, and the
SSRF, size and auth rules the host proxy must enforce before any such manifest
is accepted.

Verified from `aether-map/`: 19 new tests across `src/assets/openverse.test.ts`
and `src/panels/AssetBrowser.test.tsx`, `ruff` clean, 121 host tests passing,
and a live end-to-end run — 20 real results for "caustics", thumbnails, and an
import landing in the show as `Caustic-light.jpeg · 1024×766 · 87 kB`.

## Map: canvas drag transfers shapes between scene artboards — 2026-09-21

Releasing a moved surface over another scene's artboard now changes scene
ownership as part of the same pointer gesture. Its row moves beneath the
destination scene in Layers, its geometry is converted from the source
artboard's coordinate space so it stays under the pointer, the destination
becomes active, and the source and destination renders plus linked outputs
refresh from the new ownership. A release outside every artboard now moves the
object to the workspace root, as documented above.

A selected Cube or Box transfers all of its face surfaces atomically and keeps
its compound icon and shared group. A selected face still transfers by itself,
leaving the old compound as expected. Destination folder-name collisions get a
distinct numbered group instead of merging unrelated shapes. Movement and
reparenting are one Undo/Redo step. Selecting a layer or compound in another
scene's tree branch activates its owning scene and keeps that row selected and
movable. Layers visually stranded over a different artboard by an older build
now receive the click before the inactive artboard beneath them, allowing the
next body drag to complete the transfer and repair tree ownership.

Verified: 389 Map unit tests, production TypeScript/Vite build, lint with the
existing warnings, and all six Chrome scene workflows. The transfer coverage
includes a surface, a tree-selected five-face Box, individual face editing,
recovery of a visually stranded surface, tree reparenting, both artboards,
output routing, selection, Undo and Redo.

## Map: repeated shape editing no longer overwhelms the page — 2026-09-21

Surface body, resize, rotation, warp and compound drags can emit many immutable
document values in one gesture. The editor previously serialized the complete
show into synchronous recovery storage for every raw pointer sample while also
structured-cloning every sample to output windows. Real projects with media,
tracking data or many layers could starve the browser until the editor painted
white and needed a refresh.

The canvas still renders every interaction live. Autosave now retains the
pre-gesture snapshot while the pointer is down and serializes the final or
cancelled document once the gesture closes. Output publishing coalesces changes
to one complete show per animation frame; session handoff, hello and heartbeat
messages remain immediate. A root editor error boundary also replaces a blank
root with a themed Reopen workspace action and confirms autosave recovery.

Verified: 363 Map unit tests, production build, lint with existing warnings,
and six focused Chrome manipulation/performance flows. The stress flow creates
three shapes, performs a 60-sample drag, repeatedly moves all three, changes a
polygon through five side counts, watches renderer/page errors, and confirms
that the long gesture causes at most two recovery writes.

## Map: one content tree, and a ribbon that holds only tools — 2026-09-21

Scenes and Layers were two trees. `Scene.surfaces` already meant a layer is
nested under a scene, so they were one tree split for no structural reason.
They are now one, the way a drawing tool lists artboards with their contents
beneath them: scenes are the roots, and layers, folders, assets and the scene's
backdrop hang off whichever scene owns them. The left rail drops to Layers and
Outputs.

**Dragging a layer onto another scene moves it there** — same id, cues and
clips, so nothing pointing at it breaks, and no media migrates because a show
owns its media rather than a scene. It lands on top unless dropped before a
particular layer, joins a folder if dropped on one, and drops its old folder
otherwise, since folders belong to the scene whose layers named them. There is
a "Move to scene" command in the row menu too, because dragging across a
collapsed scene is a fiddly way to say it.

What kept the change small is the same rule the canvas already uses: touching a
row in another scene cuts to that scene first, so by the time a command runs its
scene is the active one. Layer editing needed no change at all.

`scene-tree.ts` holds the two things that are not presentation — deciding what
a row id refers to, and moving a layer between scenes — pure and tested.
Folder rows are keyed by scene now (`folder/<sceneId>/<name>`): folder names are
per scene, so "Trim" in two scenes would otherwise have been one identity.

**The ribbon holds only tools.** Undo, Redo, Save, Import SVG, Export and
"Download mapping as SVG" act on the show rather than on whatever you have
pointed at, so they moved to the header's document menu alongside Rename and
Save a copy, with their shortcuts shown. Add Media and Transparent PNG stayed —
they create a surface. New Output and Devices stayed — they are output setup.

The right rail keeps every tool it had: Program, Transform, Color, Output,
Scene setup and Properties. Properties follows the selection (surface, scene,
asset, backdrop) and deliberately does *not* re-mount Transform, Color or Output,
which have their own panels — two live copies of one editor made every locator
that reached for them ambiguous, and read as duplication rather than
consolidation.

Two defects the work surfaced, both fixed rather than worked around: clicking
the row of the scene you were already on reported nothing, so the one toolbar
stayed pointed at a layer while a scene row was highlighted; and
`defaultOpenLeft` still named the deleted `scenes` panel, which silently broke
which panels opened.

Also gone: the "no surfaces yet" placeholder. Scenes are the tree's roots, so
the tree is never empty — an empty scene reads as a scene row with nothing under
it.

Verified from `aether-map/`: `npm test` 362 passing, `npm run build` green,
`npm run lint` 0 errors, `npx playwright test` 90 passed / 2 failed — the two
being `launcher.spec.ts` (reads `.library-top` with no wait, fails on a cold dev
server) and `video.spec.ts` (drives Timeline widgets without `openTimeline`),
both red before this work and both with a one-line fix proven in
`dev/briefings/2026-09-19-map-artboard-canvas.md`.

## Map: editable polygon sides and scene-isolated artboards — 2026-09-20

Polygon-tool surfaces now expose a Sides property (3–64) in Properties and
the feature window. Changing it regenerates the regular outline around its
current centre and first-vertex direction without changing the warp quad or
content. New polygons save their side count; the parser recognizes older
six-point regular polygon outlines. Resetting to a quad or adding a freeform
point removes the regular-polygon setting.

Dragging a surface between scenes updates the tree and both artboards. Mapping
artboards now show only their own scene even while Program is crossfading; the
output window still renders the blended program. This removes the apparent
ghost on the source artboard after a layer moves to the crossfade target.

Verified: 362 Map unit tests, Map production build, lint with existing
warnings, and two focused Chrome scene/crossfade flows.

## Map: Cube and Box groups have their own Layers icons — 2026-09-20

Cube and Box group rows in Layers now use distinct shape glyphs; ordinary
user-created folders retain the folder glyph. Each generated face persists its
compound shape identity in the show, so the icon survives save/reopen and
folder renaming. Explicitly moving a face into a different folder clears that
identity. Shows created before this field existed recover Cube/Box identity
when their folder contains the exact original face set; explicit regrouping is
recorded so a later reload will not misidentify a manual folder.

Verified: 355 Map unit tests, Map build, and six focused Chrome Add Shape flows
including Cube, Box and an ordinary folder icon.

Placing a Cube or Box now selects its folder instead of the first face. On the

## Map: one Properties panel that follows the selection, and a Program panel — 2026-09-20

The right rail had five panels — Transform, Color, Output, Scene setup and
Properties — that all answered questions about the same selected thing, and you
had to know which one to open. It now has **two**.

**Properties answers for whatever you selected last.** Select a surface and you
get its name, shape, transform, appearance, content, corners and outline in one
panel. Select a scene and you get the scene: name, artboard size, timeline
length, hidden, suppressed, which outputs are projecting it, and its setup
backdrop. Select an output and you get its device, its scene link and its crop.
Select an asset and you get its timing and source *plus* the transform and
appearance of the layer it sits on — an asset has no geometry of its own, and
losing the layer's would have been a capability the consolidation took away.

Making that work needed one new thing. Layers, Scenes and Outputs each keep
their own selection, so "what is selected" was genuinely ambiguous; `App` now
records which tree you touched last and the panel switches on that. A related
fix fell out of it: clicking the row of the scene you are already on used to
report nothing at all, because the tree suppressed it to avoid a redundant cut.
It reports every click now, and the *caller* decides that only a different scene
is a cut.

Merging the panels exposed one real duplication and removed it. `CommonFields`
and `TransformPanel` each drew a lock button and an "Align to scene" row for the
same `surface.locked` and the same layer — invisible while they were separate
panels, absurd once they were adjacent sections, and spelled two different ways
("Centre" against "Center"). Transform keeps them.

**The crossfader moved out of the Scenes tray into a new Program panel.** It was
read as an unexplained opacity slider, which is what an unlabelled control parked
under a tree looks like — a tree lists what a show *contains*, so anything
beneath one reads as belonging to a row. It is not a property of a scene at all;
it is a live instrument. Properties would have been the wrong home too, for the
opposite reason: a selection-driven panel would take the fader away the instant
you clicked a surface, which is exactly when you are mid-show. So it has its own
always-available panel, now labelled as a crossfade, with A and B named at both
ends and a line that says what is actually going out. Blackout and the output
test grid joined it: they were buried in Output properties behind selecting an
output, and they are the other two things you reach for during a show.

Scene properties still have their dialog — creating a scene has no selection for
a panel to follow — but the dialog and the panel now render one shared
`SceneSizeFields`, so the five interlocking size controls cannot drift apart.

Verified from `aether-map/`: `npm test` 333 passing across 37 files (5 new
`ProgramPanel` tests, 5 new selection tests in `App.test.tsx`), `npm run build`
green, `npm run lint` 0 errors, `npx playwright test` 87 passed / 1 failed —
that one being `video.spec.ts`, which drives Timeline widgets without calling
the `openTimeline` helper and has been red since the 2026-09-18 Surfaces-tab
change.

Worth knowing for anyone running the browser suite: the e2e host serves

the specs test the previous build.

## Map: the canvas stays where you put it — 2026-09-20

Jonathan: "I should be able to move my render view where I want and work, but
every time I edit a surface the render view snaps back to a default location."

It did, and the path was short. `bounds` is derived from the document, so it was
a new object on every edit. `fit` depended on it, so `fit` was a new callback on
every edit. The resize-observer effect depended on `fit`, so it tore down and
rebuilt on every edit — and its first act was `autoFitRef.current = true`,
throwing away the operator's manual pan and zoom, followed immediately by a
refit. Nudge a corner, and the canvas jumped back to the default. Every keystroke
in a name field did it too.

Three changes, one idea — *editing the show is not a request to move the canvas*:
`bounds` is read through a ref so `fit` is stable and the observer is set up once
at mount; auto-fit is armed at the ref's initial value and after that only by the
Fit control; and a separate effect refits on the *value* of the bounds changing —
a new scene, a resized artboard — so a view that is still the automatic one
follows the show while a placed one is left alone.

The shared `maybeFit` also carries the guard the old observer had and the new
effect first lacked: a host that has not been laid out fits to nothing and leaves
a degenerate scale behind that every coordinate conversion inherits. Five unit
tests caught exactly that, in jsdom, where a host is always 0×0.

Covered by `e2e/viewport.spec.ts`: pan the canvas, then change a layer's opacity,
drag a warp corner, and add a surface — the transform is identical after each —
and Fit still returns to the default.

Also fixed here: `show.spec.ts` reaches for a cue button on the timeline, which
is not mounted now that Mapping opens on the Surfaces tray; it opens the timeline
first, like the other specs.

Validation: 317 Map unit tests, the theme-literal guard, TypeScript, the Map
build, and 14 browser tests across viewport, artboards, layout, show,
manipulation, transforms and surfaces.

## Map: the Surfaces tray reads as tiles, and carries the backdrop — 2026-09-19

Jonathan, with the reference app side by side: the tray looked wrong in dark
mode, the add button was a document glyph rather than a plain plus, the tray was
taller than it needed to be, and the backdrop photo was missing from it.

**The tiles were punched out of the tray instead of sitting on it.** They were
filled with `bg-control`, which is *darker* than the panel in dark mode
(`#121219` on `#191922`) — so each tile read as a hole. They now use
`bg-inset`, which is lighter than the panel in dark and darker than it in light,
so one rule reads as a raised tile in both themes.

**A tile is now the shape of the artboard.** Its aspect ratio comes from the
scene, set inline, so the tile's own border *is* the scene's edge: nothing draws
a second rectangle inside the first, and where a surface sits in the room reads
correctly at 40px instead of floating in a letterbox. The subject keeps its
layer colour — the same colour as its dot, its outline and its clips — filled
properly rather than washed to a tint, and brighter again when selected.

**The backdrop has a cell, because the Layers tree has a row.** The strip was
built on `activeSurfaces` and silently dropped the scene's setup photo; it is
built on `editableLayers` now, the same list the tree shows, in the same order.
That cell draws the photograph itself rather than an outline of where it sits:
recognising the room is the whole reason it exists. This strip is that tree,
drawn instead of named — same list, same selection, same order.

**Smaller, and no longer sharing a height with the timeline.** Tray height is
remembered per workspace: a timeline needs depth to show tracks against a ruler,
the Surfaces strip is one row of tiles and anything more is empty space to look
past. Sharing one height meant whichever you set last was wrong for the other.
Surfaces defaults to 72px, the rest keep 240, and the floor dropped from 90 to
72 so the strip can be pulled down to just its tiles. New `plus` icon in the
shared pack for the add button, which is a plus and nothing else.

**Fallout fixed, not papered over.** Mapping now opens on the Surfaces tray, and
a tray renders only its active workspace — so every spec that assumed the
timeline was mounted on load was failing. `e2e/helpers.ts` gained `openTimeline`
and the specs that reach for keyframes, the ruler or clips now choose the
timeline first: `features`, `live-sources`, `surface-assets`, `artboards`.

**The tiles grow with the tray.** Dragging it taller is how you ask to see the
room better, and a fixed 40px tile answered that with more empty space. They
fill the tray's height now, and since the tile's aspect ratio is the artboard's,
the width follows on its own. It stops at 160px: at full height two tiles filled
the window and the third was off the edge, which is a worse way to find a
surface than the small ones were. Past the cap they centre in the extra room,
and the add button grows with them to a smaller ceiling — it is a button, not a
thumbnail.

Validation: 275 Map unit tests, 198 UI tests, the theme-literal and icon-pack
guards, TypeScript and all five web builds. `surfaces.spec.ts` passes, including
a case that measures a tile at three tray heights.

**Known red, deterministic, not from this change:** `authoring.spec.ts:4` and
`artboards.spec.ts:9` both fail the same way — after switching scenes, the
output window keeps showing the previous scene (0 surfaces expected, 1 seen;
1280px expected, 540px seen). The output session, channel and link are all
healthy (`data-link="live"`, matching `doc-` sessions), so this is not the
hand-off regression fixed on the 16th. Reverting this change's App edits does
not fix it. It sits in scene switching and lives beside another writer's recent
scene-mix/crossfade work. `player.spec.ts:15` also fails on the Pi daemon's own
page URL, which is outside the editor entirely.

## Map: every scene on the canvas, and outputs that say what they show — 2026-09-19

The canvas drew one scene at a time. It now draws them all, side by side, the
way a drawing tool lays out artboards — you can see the shape of a show without
cutting between its scenes to remember what is in them.

**Only the artboard you are editing is interactive.** A press on any other
focuses it first; then it behaves exactly as the single scene always did. That
one rule is why the change is small: `activeScene()` still means one scene, so
hit testing, the transform and crop overlays, the corner and mask handles, the
drawing tools, the timeline and the properties panel are untouched. The pointer
path gained a single subtraction — the active artboard's origin — in
`SurfaceCanvas`'s `toRaster`.

Layout is computed, not stored (`artboards.ts`): a row in scene order, with the
Scenes panel's reorder as the way to move one. An artboard's position on a
canvas means nothing to a projector, so there is no position to save or migrate.
`Fit` now fits the whole show; `100%` centres the scene you are editing, since
at true size a multi-scene show is wider than any screen. Artboard names are
counter-scaled, so they stay legible at any zoom.

**Hide and suppress are different things**, and a scene row now carries both as
pinned icons — the same `dimmed` + `actions` mechanism the Layers panel already
used, not a third way of saying "off". Hide is editor-only: off the canvas,
still playing, still cuttable, and absolute enough to include the scene you are
on. Suppress takes a scene out of the *show* — no output renders it, the
crossfader will not fade to it — while it stays on the canvas and stays
editable, because a scene you are still building is exactly the scene you
suppress. Enforced in one place, `sceneLayers`, which every path to a wall goes
through.

**An output renders only the scene it is linked to.** Unbound means dark:
nothing is connected to it, so there is nothing to show. It no longer follows
the active scene — that fallback was right while the canvas drew one scene and
became a hazard the moment it drew all of them, because `activeSceneId` now
means "the artboard I am editing" and a projector tracking it would repaint the
wall whenever someone clicked a different artboard mid-show. Three paths keep
working shows lit: outputs are created bound, an output whose scene is deleted
is rebound to the scene that replaces it, and opening an older file binds its
unbound outputs to the scene that was active when it was saved.

That last one is why the show format is now **version 3**. An unbound output
writes no `sceneId` either way, so the field cannot tell a deliberately dark
output from a pre-version-3 one — the file's version is what distinguishes
them. Versions 1 and 2 still open, and their outputs come up showing what they
showed when they were saved.

Verified from `aether-map/`: `npm test` 301 passing across 35 files (9 new
canvas artboard tests, 14 new layout tests in `artboards.test.ts`, 3 new output
binding tests), `npm run build` green, `npm run lint` with no errors and no new
warnings.

Not done: viewport culling. Every artboard renders live, so a show pays N sets
of video decodes. Shows have a handful of scenes, so this is a real but small
cost; `artboardLayout` already returns the boxes a cull would test. Marked with
a `ponytail:` comment at the call site.

## Map: the Surfaces workspace — the scene as a row of cells — 2026-09-18

The bottom tray had Assets, Timeline, Audio and Export. It now leads with
**Surfaces**, and it is the tab that answers the question you actually ask
standing in front of a wall.

The Layers tree lists names in paint order: what the scene contains, nested,
ordered, with its commands. That is the right tool for structure and the wrong
one for recognition — "Surface 4" tells you nothing about which rectangle on the
building it is. Each cell in the strip draws **the whole scene** at thumbnail
size and lights up the one surface it stands for, in that surface's own layer
colour, with every other surface behind it in outline. The fourth rectangle from
the left is now the one that looks like the fourth rectangle from the left.

Drawn in scene pixels and scaled by the SVG viewBox, so a cell needs no layout
arithmetic and the arrangement stays true whatever the artboard is;
`vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke` keeps hairlines hairline, since a 1920-wide
viewBox in a 104px cell would otherwise render a 1px stroke at a twentieth of a
pixel. Geometry is animated at the playhead, so a strip at 15 s shows where
things are at 15 s.

Picking a cell is the editor's one selection — the Layers tree, the canvas and
the strip always agree, in both directions. Double-clicking opens the surface,
as the trees do. A hidden surface keeps its cell, dimmed and marked, because a
surface you cannot see is exactly the one you go looking for; it drops out of
the *other* cells' context, which show what projects. An empty scene says so and
offers the way out of being empty.

**Semantics:** a labelled group of buttons carrying `aria-current`, not a
listbox. A listbox promises arrow-key navigation with roving focus, and claiming
the role without honouring it is worse for a screen reader than plain buttons
Tab already reaches. `aria-current` is how the rest of the suite marks the
current row.

Covered by `e2e/surfaces.spec.ts`: a cell per surface, each drawing the scene
with one subject and the rest as context; selection round-trips with the Layers
tree; hiding is reflected both ways; the strip follows the active scene; and the
empty state adds the first surface.

Validation: 271 Map unit tests, the theme-literal and icon-pack guards,
TypeScript and the Map build. Host restarted.

Not changed: Timeline is still the tray's default tab, so the strip mounts only
when chosen and cannot affect anything that does not open it.

## Map: the projector never loses its editor, and the suite is green — 2026-09-16

Second pass over Aether Map's quality. The fifteen browser specs left red
yesterday turned out to be hiding two real defects, not just drift. All 56 Map
browser tests pass now, from 19 failing.

**A projector stopped following the show the moment autosave named it.** An
unsaved show's output channel is a per-tab draft id; once autosave gives the
show a document id the channel becomes `doc-<id>`. The window already aimed at
the projector went on listening to the draft name — it held whatever frame it
had when the save landed, and every later edit, scene change included, reached
only the editor. In a venue that is a projector stuck on the previous scene
while the operator drives a show it cannot see. The editor now hands its windows
over: it announces the new session on the old channel, the window follows it and
rewrites its own URL so a reload lands there too, and the old channel stays open
and fed for the life of the editor, so a window that missed the hand-off keeps
playing the current render rather than a stale frame. The window is renamed at
the same time, or reopening an output after a reload would have stacked a second
window beside the one on the projector. Covered by `output-session.test.tsx` and
by a new `output-link.spec.ts` case that opens a window on a draft, lets autosave
name the show and watches the window follow.

**An output could not change its device while its window was open.** Switching
an output from Monitor to Cast re-focused the monitor window instead of opening
the Cast tab: the window was reused by output id, with no notion of which
transport it was serving. An output has one device, so moving it now closes the
window it was playing on and opens the new one — a Cast tab cannot be a reused
popup anyway, which is where Chrome keeps the Cast menu.

**Matching a display resized the wrong raster** (yesterday's finding, fixed):
"Match window size" and "Match display size" wrote `show.output` while the
picker, crop fields, preview and surfaces all read the active scene's artboard.
Matching now resizes the artboard through `patchScene`.

**The specs themselves.** Twelve reached for commands that the shared
`CollectionFooter` puts behind "More …" — it keeps only "New folder" and the
create command in view, by design. Rather than fix that twelve times, `e2e/helpers.ts`
grew `command`/`runCommand`/`openCommands`, which find a collection command
wherever it lives, and `openPanel`/`openOutputProperties`, which encode that a
rail panel button is a toggle and that an output's device is a property of the
selected output. The shader picker is a `MenuButton`, not a `<select>`, so the
27-effect sweep drives the menu; "Output region" became the Output properties
panel; "Move output crop" became "Move output region"; and Tracker content
appends to the selected surface instead of making its own, so the live-camera
test gives it a surface of its own.

Validation: 254 Map unit tests, 198 UI tests, 112 host tests, 1208 aether_animation
tests, **56 Map browser tests (all passing)**, ruff, the theme-literal and
icon-pack guards, TypeScript, and all five web builds. The local host was
restarted on the new builds.

## Map output: one window per output, and never a stale stream — 2026-09-15

Two output windows could be alive at once, the older one still animating while
the newer held the current state. The cause was the output session id:

```ts
const [session] = useState(() => crypto.randomUUID());
```

It was minted on every editor mount, and it names both the BroadcastChannel and
the output window. Reloading the editor therefore changed both: the window
already aimed at the projector went on listening to a channel nobody published
to — running its own clock forward from a stale transport anchor, which is why
it looked like the live one — while the next Open, now using a different window
name, created a second window beside it.

**The session now follows the document.** A saved show's session is derived from
its document id, so every editor open on that show addresses the same channel
and the same window name: reopening an output from another tab, or after a
reload, targets the window already on that projector instead of stacking one
beside it. An unsaved show falls back to a per-tab id held in `sessionStorage`,
which survives its own reload, and different documents still never share a
channel — the isolation the session id existed for.

**An output that loses its editor stops.** Editors now publish on a 2s heartbeat
as well as on every change, so silence means something; an output that has heard
nothing for 7s holds its last frame instead of running its clock on, and says
"Not linked to an editor — holding its last frame". A projector confidently
animating a state nobody holds any more is worse than one that admits it.
Deployed devices have no editor and are exempt. The output root carries
`data-link="live" | "lost"`, which the browser tests assert and which is
diagnosable on a projector.

Covered by `aether-map/e2e/output-link.spec.ts`: the session survives an editor
reload; an output whose editor is closed goes to `lost` and shows the notice;
and two editors on one saved document both feed a single output window, which
stays live when one of them closes. `output-session.test.tsx` covers the
identity rules including blocked storage.

Validation: 253 Map unit tests, 198 UI tests, 111 host tests, 18 browser tests
across output-link, tray, details, sidebar and launcher, the theme guard,
TypeScript and the Map build.

Not claimed: a window opened by hand at an output URL for a different session is
still its own window; the guarantee is that the editor never opens a second one
and that an unfed output stops playing.

## Suite tray: a truthful connection light — 2026-09-15

The bottom tray carried the workspace name beside "Aether Studio" on the left
and the signed-in person plus an appearance toggle on the right. It now leads
with a connection light beside "Aether Studio", puts the workspace name on the
right, and carries neither identity nor theme control — both already live in
the header.

The light reports what the host actually says. Green when `/api/status`
answers and the installation is ready; amber when it answers but setup is
unfinished or the server cannot write its storage; red when it cannot be
reached at all; grey before the first answer lands. It re-checks every 15
seconds and immediately on `online`, `offline` and tab visibility, so it
recovers after a sleep or a dropped network rather than waiting out the
interval. Nothing here invents a health signal the server does not send —
those are the only states `/api/status` supports today.

The same check now feeds the Studio page's sidebar indicator, which read
`<StatusDot kind="ok" /> Local host connected` with the state hardcoded: it
claimed a healthy connection whether or not there was one. Both indicators
share one `useConnection` hook so they cannot disagree.

Removing the appearance toggle from the tray would have left the seven library
homes with no light/dark control — it exists in the Map and CAD editors and the
coming-soon homes, but was not in the library header. It now sits beside the
account chip there, the arrangement `ComingSoonHome` already uses. The signed-in
person is unaffected: the account chip carries it in the header, and the Studio
page's sidebar carries its own profile row.

Covered by `aether-map/e2e/tray.spec.ts` in Chrome: the dot precedes the name
and reads green with a "Connected" tooltip, the workspace name sits on the right
with no button or identity in the tray while both remain in the header, and —
the test that matters — cutting `/api/status` off turns the light red within the
poll interval and restoring it turns the light green again.

Validation: 197 UI tests, 111 host tests, 15 browser tests across tray, details,
sidebar and launcher, the theme guard, TypeScript and all seven builds.

## Shared sidebar: rail rows now share one icon column — 2026-09-15

Follow-up to the rail-width fix earlier today, and the same defect one level
deeper. With the rail finally narrowing, its rows did not line up: the four
navigation icons sat 10px right of every other row and their rows overflowed
the rail by 10px, measured in Chrome — icon centres at 38 against a rail centre
of 28, rows 56px wide in a 56px rail with 10px of padding on each side.

The shared row contract and the consumer's own rule are both specificity
(0,1,2) — `.aui-sidebar nav button` against `.library-nav nav button` — so the
consumer, later in the bundle, won. Its expanded `padding: 11px 10px` and
`gap: 10px` therefore stayed applied in the rail, stacking on top of the icon's
own `margin: 0 10px`. The row contract now carries a doubled class so it wins
on its own, as the rail width does.

The Workspaces rows had a second, smaller problem: they sit outside `<nav>` and
were never marked `.aui-sidebar-row`, so they missed the shared geometry and
rendered "New workspace…" at the icon's natural 13px among 16px neighbours.
They now declare the shared row class, which is what it is for, rather than
being hand-matched in product CSS.

Every rail row — Create, the collapse toggle, all four navigation rows, the
workspace tile and New workspace — now centres at exactly 28 in a 56px rail on
both `/map/` and `/cad/`, with no row overflowing.

`aether-map/e2e/sidebar.spec.ts` gains an alignment test per application: every
row's icon centre within a pixel of the rail's centre, no row overflowing, and
each icon inside one slot's size range so a row rendering at its natural size
stands out. It waits for the width transition to settle first — an earlier
version measured mid-animation and reported a 1.3px error that was the test's
own race, not the product's. Confirmed to fail on the previous CSS with
`Received: 10`, the overflow.

Validation: 193 UI tests, 217 Map unit tests, 110 host tests, 5 sidebar browser
tests, ruff, the theme guard, TypeScript and all seven production builds.

## Shared sidebar: the collapsed rail now actually shrinks — 2026-09-15

The application home pages collapsed their sidebar's labels but never its
width, leaving a 210px column of empty space with the icons floating in it.

The cause was a CSS cascade defect in the shared component, not in any product.
`@aether/ui` declared the rail as `.aui-sidebar--collapsed { width: 56px }` —
one class, specificity (0,1,0) — while a consumer sets its own expanded width
with its own single class, later in the bundle. At equal specificity the later
rule wins, so the consumer's expanded width silently beat the shared rail. Both
other consumers had independently worked around it by restating the rule with
two classes (`.aui-coming-nav.aui-sidebar--collapsed`,
`.gallery-sidebar.aui-sidebar--collapsed`); `library.css` had not, which is why
the gallery collapsed correctly and every application home did not.

The shared rule now carries both classes so it wins on its own, and normalises
its side padding, so the rail is exactly one icon slot wide whatever padding a
consumer uses when expanded — `library-nav`'s 14px sides would otherwise have
squeezed the icons out of a 56px rail. The two consumer workarounds are now
redundant but harmless and were left in place.

Guarded by `aether-map/e2e/sidebar.spec.ts` in real Chrome on `/map/` and
`/cad/`: the rail must be narrow rather than merely label-less, its icons must
stay inside it, expanding must restore the width, and the preference must
survive a reload while staying per-application. jsdom cannot catch this — it
applies no stylesheets — so the browser test is the only thing that could have.
Confirmed it fails on the old rule with `Received: 210`.

Validation: 193 UI tests, 217 Map unit tests, 110 host tests, ruff, the theme
guard and all seven production builds pass; every bundle ships the corrected
rule. The full Map e2e suite went from 17 failures to 14 — the difference is
exactly the three new sidebar tests. The remaining 14 pre-date this work and
are unrelated: they assert UI that does not exist yet (a "Move layer forward"
button, a "Show size" readout), verified by reverting this change and seeing
them fail identically.

## Default autosave and readable Map filenames — 2026-09-14

Map, hosted CAD Parts/Assemblies and Animation now use `core/session/autosave.ts`
for always-on saving and refresh recovery. Products retain their own serializer,
canonical engine and revision-checked host APIs. A pending snapshot is stored in
this tab before the delayed server write; only one save runs at a time, and an
older response cannot clear a newer edit. Network failures retry, while revision
and permission failures retain work without silently overwriting server changes.
Recovery is scoped by account/document/tab (plus CAD project item/branch/revision).
New Map shows and CAD workspaces save without requiring a manual first Save.

Map's filename receives available header space, remains clickable for rename and
has a full-name tooltip. Its header shows actual save state and offers Save a copy
for conflicts/read-only files. Feature/Backdrop previews remain recoverable while
server saving is paused, then resume on Accept or restore on Discard. Opening a
show waits for its recovery decision; canvas sizing attaches after that load.
CAD obtains immediate Part snapshots and canonical Assembly archives, restores
pending documents on refresh, and shows Autosave as always on in settings.
Animation captures accepted rig edits and saves through its engine serializer.

Recovery uses sessionStorage: it survives refresh in that tab, not closing the
last copy or clearing browser storage. Completed server saves remain durable.
Unavailable/full storage and incomplete Assembly capture retain navigation
protection until server saving/capture succeeds. Unsubmitted tool-dialog input
and edits not yet accepted by a product engine are not committed documents.
Sketch/Vector remain placeholders without editable file workflows. Existing tabs
must save once before reloading to receive the new autosave implementation.

Verified: 207 Map unit tests, 19 targeted CAD host/Assembly/document tests, and all
three product production builds. Nineteen distinct isolated Chrome workflows
passed across immediate/new-document refresh, offline API recovery, delayed-save
races, conflict/copy recovery, CAD Part and Assembly persistence, Animation mate
persistence, header, artboards, scene tree, Backdrop, transform/color, timeline
media, video and the real local player. Final Map regression run: 11/11 passed.
Map lint has no errors: three existing effect warnings and six React Compiler
memoization warnings in App. Filename, Map layout and CAD/Animation recovery
screenshots reviewed. Production frontend bundles rebuilt; no production host
restart or user document writes were needed.

## Map: standard Select/Node controls, Backdrop, Transform and Color — 2026-09-14

Every Map asset uses a common Select box: body dragging, eight circular resize
handles with directional cursors, and a rotation handle above the selection.
Corners resize two axes; side handles resize one axis unless aspect locking is
on. Shift preserves proportions; Shift-rotation snaps to 15° increments. Snap
aligns scene/layer edges and centers with guides; Alt bypasses it. The separate
Sketch → Node (A) tool exposes individual quad corners and existing outline
points. Sketch → Select (V) restores the normal transform box. Tool activation
returns keyboard focus to the canvas, so pan/selection shortcuts work immediately.

Right-side Transform provides X/Y, width/height, aspect lock, relative Scale by,
rotation and scene alignment for any selected layer. Geometry edits move masks
with their quad and account for the evaluated animation transform without changing
its keys. Color supplies source-color editing, swatches and opacity for fill,
text, tracker and shader palettes; the layer-marker color is labeled separately.
Image/video content retains its own colors.

The setup image is now **Backdrop**, with a shared image icon, a bottom layer row,

## Aether Map: rooms, layer colours, clips on tracks — 2026-09-13

**Rooms.** The top of the app is now the shared `DocumentBar` with a `Tabs`
switcher in its centre, as Aether Animation switches workspaces: **Mapping**
(scenes, layers, properties, devices around the canvas) and **Sequence**
(assets and layers in the rail, properties, and a taller timeline). Same
document, different layout. Each room is its own `WorkspaceShell` keyed and
stored separately, so each remembers its own panel arrangement. The bar carries

**Layer colour.** Every layer has an identity colour — its dot in the list,
its outline and handles on the canvas, its clips on the timeline — assigned
in turn from a palette as layers are created and editable in Properties. It is
distinct from what the layer projects; the colour fill from earlier remains
the content.

**Clips on tracks.** The timeline is now one track per layer, each holding
clips in sequence the way a video editor's does. Place an asset from the
Assets panel onto the selected layer at the playhead: a video takes its own
length, an image holds for ten seconds. Drag a clip to move it, its edges to
trim it; clips snap to tenths and to neighbours' edges, and trimming the start
moves the asset's in-point with it so the picture does not jump. A clip loops
its asset across its span or holds the last frame. A layer with clips shows
whichever clip covers the playhead and **nothing** in a gap; a layer without
clips shows its static source as before, so every existing show plays exactly
as it did. Cues sit on the same tracks as diamonds. The show file gains
`clips` and `color` per surface; older files open with colours by position.

The clip timeline is product code in `aether-map/src/panels/ClipTimeline.tsx`
rather than the shared `Timeline`, which is keyframe-only; the arithmetic —
placement, move, trim, snap, in-point, loop — is pure and tested in
`clips.ts`. If Animation wants clip tracks too, that is the candidate for
promotion to `@aether/ui`.
