198 shared UI tests, typecheck, and the UI, CAD, Map, Animation and Studio builds
pass. No browser was available, so the rendered surfaces are not claimed.

## Suite chrome: a settings gear, and a OneDrive-shaped account menu — 2026-09-15

The account slot (`[data-aether-account]`, present in every front end — CAD,
Animation, Map, the library homes, ComingSoonHome, the gallery) now renders two
controls instead of one, both from the single shared web component in
`core/session/account.js` that the host injects into every page's head.

**The gear.** A settings popover carrying Theme — a native `<select>` for Follow
system / Light / Dark — and a **Settings** item. That item dispatches a
cancelable `aether-open-settings` event: an app whose own `SettingsWindow`
listens calls `preventDefault()` and opens it, and anything else falls through to
Studio's settings page. Map claims it; the rest fall back. A product wires its
settings window in with one `useEffect`.

**Appearance is now bootstrapped, not mounted.** `aether-appearance`
(localStorage) and the `.aether-light-theme` class had exactly one writer:
`AppearanceToggle`, a React component in `@aether/ui`. A page that never mounted
one — the library home, for instance — therefore loaded in dark mode no matter
what the member had chosen, because nothing re-applied the class after
navigation. The shared module now reads the key and applies the class at load,
before any React app mounts, and follows `prefers-color-scheme` changes while
the mode is "system". `AppearanceToggle` keeps its own control but both sides
emit and listen for an `aether-appearance` event, so the gear and the toggle
cannot disagree on the same screen.

**The account menu** follows OneDrive's shape: the suite brand (a link home) and
Sign out on one line, then a 76px avatar, full name, email and View account. The
name no longer sits beside the avatar in the bar — the avatar alone is the
control, as in the reference.

**Shared icons over HTTP.** The widget is vanilla JS outside any bundler, so it
could not reach `AetherIcon`'s artwork, and copying the gear's geometry into it
would have been a second copy of a shared asset. `/suite/icons/<name>.svg` now
serves `core/assets/icons/` beside the existing `/suite/account.{js,css}` fast
path — public, since the chrome loads before a session exists — and the widget
fetches and inlines the real file so `stroke="currentColor"` still inherits. The
name is matched against `[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*`, so a traversal or an
alternate-cased name is a 404, covered by
`test_suite_icons_serve_shared_artwork_and_refuse_escapes`.

111 host tests, 197 shared UI tests, ruff over `core/`, and the Studio, UI, Map,
CAD and Animation builds all pass. The Map e2e header spec asserts the account
slot contains the member's name; the name moved into the (closed, still
rendered) menu, which `toContainText` reads — but no live host was available to
run that spec, so it is unverified rather than claimed.

## Library home: one listing card, details tray inside it — 2026-09-15

The file list and its column header now sit on one bordered, rounded surface
(`--aether-color-bg-panel` — near-white in light mode against the `bg-app` grey
page), the way OneDrive presents its table. Rows run flush to the card edge, and
the last row drops its rule. `.library-main` became a flex column so the card
grows to the bottom of the view rather than stopping under the last row; a short
list leaves empty card below it, and the empty state centres in that space.

The Details tray left the window and became a second card beside the first. It
was the third column of the `.library-root` grid — a full-height rail from the
top bar to the footer, opening and closing by swinging that column between
`255px` and `0px`. It is now a 290px sibling of the list card inside
`.library-listing`, separated by a 12px gap, stretching only to the listing row's
height. The toolbar's Details button still toggles it; below 800px it stacks
under the list card instead of becoming a window-bottom drawer.

**Rows.** The table no longer borrows the design system's solid selection fill
(`--aether-color-bg-selected` + white text), which reads as a modal highlight.
A selected row is now a 14% wash of `--aether-color-accent` with a 3px
`--aether-color-selection-edge` bar down its left edge, so the row's own text
colour survives; hover is `bg-row-hover`, and hovering the selected row deepens
the wash to 22%. Both cross-fade over 110ms. Grid tiles keep the solid fill.

Clicking the selected row now clears the selection instead of re-selecting it,
and clicking the card's empty space below the last row clears it too — the
handler fires only when the click lands on the card itself, so grid tiles and
row internals are unaffected. The inner name button lost its redundant click
handler; it would otherwise have toggled a second time and cancelled the first.

This is `studio/src/LibraryHome.tsx` and `studio/src/library.css`, so it lands on
every product home Studio renders — CAD, Animation, Map — at once. The table is
not a `@aether/ui` component; it is local to `LibraryHome`. Theme-literal check,
typecheck and the Studio build pass. No browser was available, so rendered
measurements are not claimed.

## Aether Map: canvas pan and zoom, resizable timeline — 2026-09-13

**Pan and zoom.** The canvas had neither. The raster was also mispositioned and
clipped, because it was centred with flex while being shrunk by
`transform: scale()` — a scaled element still occupies its full unscaled box in
layout, so the centring was computed from 1920×1080 regardless of the zoom. The
view is now an explicit `translate(x, y) scale(s)` with `transform-origin: 0 0`,
which fixes the placement and makes panning possible at the same time.

Scrolling zooms about the pointer, so whatever is under the cursor stays under
it — zoom that drifts away from the thing being aligned is useless for the job.
Pinch arrives as ctrl+wheel and is damped so a trackpad and a mouse feel alike;
Shift+wheel nudges sideways. Panning is space-drag or middle-drag, with a grab
cursor. Fit, 100% and a live zoom readout sit in the corner, and F fits.

The wheel listener is bound natively rather than through React's `onWheel`,
which is passive and cannot `preventDefault` — without that the page scrolls
instead of the canvas zooming.

**Resizable timeline.** The timeline was a fixed strip in the shell's bottom
slot. Canvas and timeline are now a vertical `SplitPane` from `@aether/ui` with
a draggable, keyboard-operable separator. `SplitPane` fixes its *primary* pane
in pixels, so the pixel value it holds is derived from the timeline height
rather than stored directly — the canvas takes the slack when the window
changes, instead of the timeline growing. The height is remembered per viewer
in `localStorage`, guarded so blocked storage cannot fail an edit.

The viewport arithmetic lives in `aether-map/src/viewport.ts`, pure and tested
away from the DOM: fit, actual size, zoom-about-cursor in both directions and
from an offset view, clamping that does not drift when a zoom is refused at the
limit, and wheel deltas converted from lines and pages so a mouse wheel does not
feel dead.

Validation: 87 aether-map tests (12 new viewport, 3 new canvas DOM), 109 host
tests, 177 UI tests, ruff, oxlint, the theme guard, TypeScript and every
production build pass.

Not claimed: no browser was driven. The gestures themselves — wheel, pinch,
space-drag, middle-drag, separator drag — are unverified by execution.

## Safari tab icons across the suite — 2026-09-13

Every app now advertises one dedicated 16/32/48px ICO generated from its current
rounded PNG logo. Hosted pages use app-specific content-hashed ICO filenames;
Apple-touch icons, app chrome and manifests retain the same full-size PNG
identity. Conventional `/favicon.ico`, `/<app>/favicon.ico`, PNG/Apple aliases
and old `/icons/<app>.svg` requests resolve to the current matching artwork
without authentication. Duplicate icon routing was consolidated in the public
asset path, preserving the host's unlocked asset delivery.

The screenshot showed obsolete tab icons despite the live primary PNG metadata
already matching current artwork. New ICO filenames provide a fresh resource
identity, and conventional fallback paths now work. No Safari cache was read or
cleared; the actual retained browser icons still require a page reload to assess.
The available browser tool does not expose Safari.

`build-favicons.py` generates the ICOs plus public copies and versioned HTML links
for all seven web roots. The main icon builder and macOS installer invoke it.
These copies are build derivatives, not separately authored logos. Production,
development, preview and offline pages all have an explicit local tab icon.

Verification: 109 host tests pass, including per-app home/editor metadata,
anonymous fallback requests, old SVG replacement, unknown/traversal paths and
changed-artwork filenames. All seven dev servers returned matching ICO bytes;
all seven packaged pages reference matching icons with transparent corners.
Seven builds passed at initial verification. The final packaging rebuild passed
for six apps; concurrent Map App.tsx layout edits introduced five unused-symbol
type errors, so its earlier successful build with the correct ICO was retained.
Scoped ruff, shell syntax and diff checks pass. The user-authorized host restart
completed; live checks verify all seven ICO/Apple/legacy paths and Studio's single
current favicon. Existing Map scene/text migration failures from the prior
integration note were resolved in Claude's subsequent handoff.

## Aether Map: scenes, text, project bundles and SVG geometry — 2026-09-13

An end-to-end run of the authoring process now passes 12 of 12 steps; the same
run scored 6 of 12 before this work.

**Scenes.** A show holds named scenes, each owning its surfaces and its own
length — an idle loop, a scare, a finale — with add, duplicate, rename, delete
and cut-between. Duplicating mints fresh surface and cue ids, because two
scenes sharing a surface identity would cue each other. Media stays owned by
the show, so one clip can appear in several scenes without being stored twice.
The document is now version 2; version 1 files open as a single scene carrying
their old per-show duration, so nothing saved earlier is lost.

**Text surfaces.** A surface can be filled with text instead of media — a sign,
a warning, a countdown — with size, colour and alignment. The text box is the
source rectangle, so the same homography applies and a sign reads correctly on
an angled wall.

**Project bundles.** `GET /api/map/project/<id>.zip` builds a named folder on
the server holding `show.aethermap`, `layout.json` as a device receives it,
every referenced asset under `media/`, a `README.txt` inventory, and
`wireframe.svg`. Assets that are referenced but absent produce a
`MISSING-ASSETS.txt` rather than a bundle that quietly lacks its media and
looks fine until show day. Archive paths are built from a sanitised folder name
and asset names containing separators are refused.

**SVG geometry, in and out.** The wireframe export draws one polygon per
surface with masks dashed, named by surface and grouped by scene, so the
mapping opens in any vector editor for measuring or printing. Import reads
`<polygon>`, `<rect>` and straight-line `<path>` data, scaling the drawing's
viewBox onto the projector raster: trace a building elevation in Illustrator or
Inkscape and each shape becomes a surface. Curves are reported rather than
silently approximated, since they cannot become a four-cornered quad.

**Output selector.** One dialog asks where the show should come out — a display
on this machine, or a paired device — and says what each needs rather than
failing silently when a device is offline or the show is unsaved.

On interchange: **there is no universal projection-mapping format.** MadMapper,
Resolume, HeavyM and Millumin are all proprietary and none interchange. SVG is
the real interoperability path for geometry, which is why it is what we read
and write. OSC, Art-Net/sACN, NDI and SMPTE timecode are the genuine industry
standards for control and transport, and none of them are implemented yet.

Validation: 72 aether-map tests (homography, playback, show-file including the
v1→v2 migration, masks, video sync, history, SVG import, formatting, canvas
DOM) and 100 host tests, plus ruff, oxlint, the theme guard, TypeScript and

inside it, two scenes, image, video and text surfaces, save, reopen
byte-identical, project bundle containing six files with both assets and a

## Aether Map: undo, device rename and media cleanup — 2026-09-13

**Undo/redo.** The show document is an immutable value, so history is a stack
of past values rather than command objects with inverses to keep in step.
Edits carry a coalesce key: a corner drag emits one edit per pointer move, and
without merging them one undo would step back a single pixel, so same-key edits
arriving within 900 ms collapse into one step. Undo clears the coalesce key, so
the next edit cannot merge into a restored value and quietly swallow the undo.
The stack is bounded at 100 entries. Ribbon buttons plus Cmd/Ctrl-Z and
Shift-Cmd/Ctrl-Z, which are ignored while a text field has focus.

**Device rename.** The `rename` endpoint shipped earlier with no way to call
it; the Devices panel now has the control, so a projector can be named for
where it stands rather than its machine id.

**Media cleanup.** A Media panel lists what a show carries — size, dimensions,
and how many surfaces use each file — and can remove media from the show or
delete orphaned files from the server. `DELETE /api/map/media/<name>` refuses
any file a saved show still references (409), scanning the map documents
directly; show documents are small and a local install has few, so the scan is
exact rather than a cache that can drift. The match is on the complete quoted
JSON string, so `a.png` cannot match inside `xa.png`. The cleanup button is
disabled until the document is saved and clean, because deleting files an
unsaved show still references would leave the saved copy without its pixels.

Validation: 59 aether-map tests (7 homography, 13 playback, 7 show-file, 6
masks, 7 video sync, 10 history, 2 formatting, 7 canvas DOM), 86 host tests,
177 UI tests, ruff, oxlint, the theme guard, TypeScript and every production
build pass. A live host verified deleting an orphan, refusing an in-use file
with 409, refusing traversal with 400 and an anonymous delete with 401.

Not claimed: no browser was driven and no Raspberry Pi, projector or Chromium
was involved. Undo, masks, keyboard nudging, the output window, the portal and
the installer's apt/systemd/kiosk paths are unverified by execution. Media
cleanup only offers files this editing session uploaded or opened; a file
orphaned by an earlier session is not listed as a candidate. Edge blending and
mesh warp remain unbuilt.

## Aether Map: masks, keyboard alignment and clip sync — 2026-09-13

**Masks.** A surface can carry an output-space polygon that clips it — how a
beam is kept off a window, a doorway or a neighbour's wall. Add a mask and it
starts as the surface's own quad inset so its handles are grabbable; drag the
square handles to shape it, add a point and it splits the longest edge rather
than always appending at the end. Removing the third-from-last point drops the
mask rather than leaving a two-point polygon that clips to nothing.

**Keyboard alignment.** Arrow keys nudge the selected corner or mask handle by
one pixel, Shift by ten. Aligning a beam to a real edge at three metres is a
one-pixel job and a mouse cannot do it.

**Clip sync.** Video now follows the show clock in both the editor preview and
the projector: the clip seeks when it drifts more than 0.25 s from
`showTime % clipDuration`, and plays or pauses with the transport. Previously a
`<video loop>` ran on its own clock, so the picture depended on when the page
happened to load, two devices never agreed, and restarting a show did not
restart its clips. One shared `SurfaceMedia` component serves both renderers.

**Deployable archive cut from 8.3 MB to 448 kB.** Two causes, both artwork:
`core/ui/src/AppIcon.tsx` bundled three full-size product PNGs into every
consumer (fixed by Codex, which now serves them from `/icons/`), and
`aether-map/public/favicon.png` was a 1.78 MB 1024×1024 render used as a tab
icon. The favicon is now the Aether Map mark as a 2.4 kB SVG with a 28 kB PNG
fallback, both rendered from Codex's `aether-map.svg`. The unused scaffold
asset `src/assets/hero.png` was deleted. That archive is what ships to a
projector over house wifi.

Validation: 47 aether-map tests (7 homography, 13 playback, 7 show-file, 6
masks, 7 video sync, 7 canvas DOM), 80 host tests, 177 UI tests, ruff, oxlint,
the theme guard, TypeScript and every production build pass.

Not claimed: no browser was driven and no Raspberry Pi, projector or Chromium
was involved. Masks, keyboard nudging, the output window, the portal display
and the installer's apt/systemd/kiosk paths are unverified by execution. Media
still has no delete or reference counting, so removing a surface orphans its
bytes on disk. Edge blending across projectors and mesh warp for curved
surfaces remain unbuilt.

## Aether Map: layers, cue timeline and networked devices — 2026-09-13

Aether Map is now demo-ready on a laptop and can drive networked output
devices.

**Layers.** Surfaces are an ordered stack — later paints on top — with raise,
lower, show/hide and a cue count per layer, listed topmost-first so the panel
reads like the picture looks. Reordering is buttons rather than drag-and-drop:
keyboard reachable, no dependency, and a projection show has a handful of
layers.

**Cue timeline.** A show is now a pure function of time. A cue sets a surface's
state at a moment (show, hide, opacity) and evaluation applies every cue at or
before the playhead, in time order regardless of authoring order. That maps
directly onto `@aether/ui`'s existing `Timeline` keyframes, so Aether Map uses
the suite's timeline rather than a second one that merely resembles it.
Transport is play/pause/scrub with a show duration and loop-or-hold. The editor
canvas renders the evaluated show, so what is authored at the playhead is what
the projector is showing at that instant.

**Output devices.** Pairing now completes: claiming a device burns its code and
issues it an `aether_dev_` token, which is how it authenticates from then on —
a projector never holds a person's session, and forgetting the device revokes
it immediately (verified 401). A Devices panel lists devices with online state,
last-seen, and which show each is running; it can pair by code, deploy a show,
stop it, and forget a device. Each device polls for its assignment and pulls
the layout, its media and the built application, so it runs offline and updates
by pulling the same archive again — no re-imaging, no login on the projector.

**One bundle, three roles.** The same build serves the editor, the projector
picture (`?output=1`) and the pairing screen a new device shows (`?portal=1`),
so a device deploys one archive and the warp cannot drift between them.

**UI conformance.** Every control is `@aether/ui`: `WorkspaceShell`, `Ribbon`,
`BottomPanel`, `Timeline`, `StatusBar`/`StatusDot`, `Dialog`, `FieldRow`,
`NumberField`, `SelectField`, `Slider`, `TextField`, `Button`, `IconButton`,
`EmptyState` and the shared `AetherIcon` set. `aether-map/src` was added to
`dev/check-theme-literals.mjs` and passes: the only remaining colour literal is
the projector's black, marked `literal-ok` because an unlit raster must emit no
light.

Validation: 32 aether-map tests (7 homography, 13 playback, 7 show-file, 5
canvas DOM), 80 host tests, 177 UI tests, ruff, oxlint, the theme guard,

code, claim it, deploy, pull the layout byte-identical, fetch media and a 9-file

## Aether Map: saving, media and projector output — 2026-09-13

The laptop loop works end to end: build a map of a room, save it, put an image
or video on a surface, and send it out of a second display to a projector.

**Saving.** `.aethermap` is JSON in the existing host library under app `map`.
Creating from the library home carries its scope and folder through; the editor
rewrites its URL to `?document=<id>` after the first save so the show reopens
and survives a refresh. Saves send the expected revision, so a stale write is
refused rather than silently overwriting.

**Media.** Show documents are JSON but projection media is video, and
`/api/library/` requires JSON and caps bodies at 9 MB. Media now streams to a
separate store: `PUT /api/map/media/<id>.<ext>` writes in 1 MB chunks to a
`.part` file and renames on completion, so an interrupted upload never leaves a
half-file a show would try to project; `GET` serves it back with full HTTP
Range support, which `<video>` needs to seek and which Safari needs to play at
all. Names are restricted to an id plus an allowed image/video extension, so
path traversal and executable formats are refused. 512 MB cap, and transfers
stream outside the host lock so a large upload cannot serialize other requests.

**Projector output.** A second window on the same machine renders only the
warped surfaces — no chrome, no grid, no handles, black ground — from the same
bundle in output mode, so there is one renderer and no second build to keep in
step. Editor and output sync over `BroadcastChannel`: same-origin, instant, no
server and no dependency. The output window announces itself on open and the
editor replies with the current show, so an unsaved document projects without
being saved first. Double-click goes fullscreen on the projector display.

This follows Jonathan's 2026-09-13 decision that the first output device is a
laptop on HDMI, with the Raspberry Pi edge node sequenced after a working
application. No renderer changed to accommodate it.

Validation: 19 aether-map tests (7 homography, 7 show-file round-trip, 5 canvas
DOM) and 5 new media-store tests; 69 host tests, ruff, oxlint and production
build pass. A live host confirmed create → media upload → corner edit → save →
read returns a byte-identical document, media bytes match on read-back, the
file lists in the library, and a stale revision is refused with 409. Media Range
reads were verified for full, bounded, suffix and open-ended requests, a 416 past
end of file, rejected traversal and rejected formats, and a 401 when anonymous.

Not claimed: no browser was driven. The output window, `BroadcastChannel` sync,
fullscreen and drag-to-second-display are unverified by execution — the
projector path needs a human with a projector. Media has no delete and no
reference counting, so removing a surface orphans its bytes on disk. Media is
readable by any signed-in user rather than following the show's sharing. Video
playback is not synchronized to anything; `playback.mode` is always loop.

## Aether Map Raspberry Pi provisioning and pairing — 2026-09-13

A Pi provisions itself as an Aether Map output device in one command:
`curl -sSL http://<server>:8780/api/map/install.sh | bash`.

The host serves three public, auth-free routes — `/api/map/ping`,
`/api/map/install.sh` and `/api/map/aether_player.py` — because a device being
imaged has no credentials. The installer is stamped with the address the client
actually reached the host on, taken from the Host header rather than the
configured `public_url`, which defaults to a loopback address and on a Pi would
mean the Pi itself. The installer is idempotent, installs Chromium and python3,
refuses a player download that does not parse as Python, derives a device id
from `/etc/machine-id` so reinstalling does not orphan the device, and
registers two systemd units: a system-scope sync daemon and a user-scope
Chromium kiosk bound to `graphical-session.target`.

`POST /api/map/devices/announce` is unauthenticated and bounded: a 4 KB body
cap, device ids restricted to alphanumerics plus `-_`, and a hard cap of 64
registered devices. Ownership comes only from a six-digit pairing code that
lives ten minutes, stays stable across heartbeats, rotates once expired, and is
consumed on claim. `GET /api/map/devices` requires a signed-in user and returns
401 otherwise. New `map_devices` table with a real foreign key to `users`.

`aether-player/` is now a sync agent that never draws a pixel: it announces,
reports its pairing code, and serves the deployed show to Chromium on
`127.0.0.1:8777`. It carries no supervision code — systemd restarts both units.
The former `renderer.py` (OpenCV, NumPy, a mocked `render()` that returned a
cleared buffer) and the placeholder `main.py` were deleted; their dependencies
were never in `pyproject.toml`.

Validation: 8 new device tests, 64 host tests, and ruff pass. A live host on a
spare port served all three routes, stamped the correct URL, returned a
compiling player, held one stable pairing code across repeated announcements,
and refused the device list with 401. The real daemon ran against that host,
announced, reported its code, and served a local `layout.json` over HTTP.

Not claimed: no Raspberry Pi, projector or Chromium was involved — the
installer's apt, systemd and kiosk paths are unexercised, and on-hardware frame
rate remains unverified. Deploy does not exist, so a provisioned device has an
empty `show/` and sits on a pairing portal page that is not built yet. On a
plain-http host the one-line installer pipes unauthenticated plaintext into a
shell; TLS on the host is the mitigation and the installer follows whichever
scheme the host serves.

## Aether Map warp canvas — 2026-09-13

Aether Map is a new product: projection mapping and show control. The host
already served it at `/map/`; it now has a working editor rather than a
scaffold.

Surfaces can be created, selected, hidden, renamed, deleted, and dragged by
their four corners over the projector's output raster. An assigned image or
video is warped onto the quad by a true planar homography emitted as a CSS
`matrix3d`, so the browser performs the perspective divide per pixel in
hardware. A surface without media renders a checkerboard, which makes the
perspective visible while aligning to a physical shape. Corner positions are
also editable numerically in the properties panel.

The scaffold's three.js viewport was removed. A subdivided mesh with four moved
vertices interpolates affinely across two triangles and creases straight lines
along the diagonal; `matrix3d` is correct by construction, keeps `<video>` in
the hardware compositing path, and dropped the production bundle from 719 kB to
275 kB. The accepted cost is that the warp is planar and cannot bend; the first
non-planar surface is the stated trigger to add a WebGL mesh path.

Validation: 12 aether-map tests (7 homography, 5 canvas DOM) pass, including a
projective assertion that fails if the transform degrades to affine and a
degenerate-quad case that must not emit NaN. `npm run build` and `oxlint` pass
clean; the dev server serves the app.

Not claimed: nothing persists. Saving, the host library, media upload, device
pairing, deploy and the Raspberry Pi output node are unbuilt — phases 2-4 in
`dev/docs/roadmap/Aether_Map.md`. Media is held as an in-memory object URL and
is lost on reload. No browser was driven and no projector or Pi was involved,
so on-hardware frame rate remains unverified.

## Sketch construction, selection actions and redundant inference — 2026-09-13

Sketch > Edit now includes Construction (shared dashed-line SVG, active toggle,
Q shortcut) and Delete. With no selection, Construction controls newly drawn
geometry; with a selection, it converts regular/construction geometry. Partial
path conversion isolates only selected edges, retaining exact segment/vertex
identities and explicit coincidence at new construction boundaries. Dashed
appearance remains visible when selected. Changing drawing tools clears stale
selection without losing the Construction mode.

Delete/Backspace and the ribbon Delete act on the current edges/profiles/vertices.
Deleting one path edge leaves the remaining edges, remaps surviving constraints
through the existing trim machinery, and removes constraints whose geometry was
removed. Vertex deletion removes incident edges; standalone points and circles
are removable. Projected references and spline control-handle deletion reject
visibly and atomically. Each edit is one sketch-history checkpoint; Cmd/Ctrl+Z,
Shift+Cmd/Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y use sketch history while editing. Text fields keep
normal editing keys. Selection conversion/deletion survives native save/reopen.

Vertical-line placement at an already fixed circle center could infer both a
center attachment and a redundant origin fix. The inference pass now discards
new automatic relations that introduce redundancy/conflicts, retaining authored
relations. Consistent redundant equations no longer paint all geometry red:
normal mobility colors remain, with a visible diagnostic warning controlled by
Show errors. Genuine unsatisfied constraints retain error coloring and reporting.

Validation: 31 existing editor-operation/trim/snap regression tests and engine
check pass. Full CAD run passed 755 tests/3 skips and found only the expected
catalog-count change (260→262); corrected catalog/actions rerun passes all 10,
and final keyboard-history/Dimension rerun passes all 11. Shared UI 175 tests,
typecheck/build, CAD build and Animation build pass. Approved isolated Chrome
verified the active Construction button, dashed vertical line, valid regular
vertical line from an origin-centered circle, single-line Delete and real Cmd+Z
restoration. Temporary QA edits cancelled; FreeCAD backend unchanged.

## View-relative cube arrows and upper-right roll controls — 2026-09-13

ViewCube directional nudges now rotate around the current camera's screen-up and
screen-right axes. Left/right no longer turn into roll at Top or Bottom, and the
same directions work after rolling the view and in either workspace up convention.
Curved arrows animate a 90-degree roll around the viewing axis while keeping the
eye, target and distance fixed; directional nudges also ease into their 15-degree
pose. A dedicated camera rotation module interpolates the rigid camera basis on
the render clock. Pointer/wheel navigation, explicit views and normal-to-sketch
interrupt pending motion; reduced-motion preferences apply the final pose directly.

The shared cube's two curved controls now sit together around its upper-right
corner, reusing the shared navigation SVGs. Directional arrows, the surrounding
square panel and Home retain their positions.

## Clear sketch selection with live drag feedback — 2026-09-13

Selected sketch edges and curves now use a distinct amber outline instead of a
thin blue highlight that resembled unconstrained geometry. Selected vertices use
filled amber markers; selected profile regions use the same selection color.
The selection renderer owns these styles and annotates each highlight with its
contour/entity identity, while existing entity references remain authoritative.

Window/crossing drags highlight candidate geometry as the rectangle moves. This
preview leaves the committed selection untouched until release, supports additive
selection, and restores the prior highlights when cancelled. Released selections
persist through the generated click and pointer movement. Multiple closed profile
boundaries select their individual edges for downstream tools.

workspace integration cases for multi-profile persistence and vertex/additive

selection counts, and a vertex-only filled marker. QA sketch cancelled afterward.

## Space preview preserves the scene and eases backward — 2026-09-13

Space no longer hides reference geometry or finished sketch curves. Its transparent
world-origin cube encloses visible bodies, reference/construction planes, finished
sketches, feature/history previews and the full active sketch surface. Hidden or
suppressed descendants do not inflate the fit, and visibility flags stay unchanged.
The ground/background remains visible without defining the finite cube bounds.

Entering the preview eases the camera position and target over 420 ms, preserving
view direction and roll instead of cutting to the wider view. It never reduces the
current viewing distance. The normal render loop updates both the 3D scene and live
sketch surface together; near/far clipping covers the transition. Pointer/wheel
input interrupts the motion, closing cancels it and restores the saved camera,
and reduced-motion preferences use an immediate transition.

passes. Approved isolated Chrome verification used real Space input: recorded

cube. The temporary preview was closed afterward.

Right-drag uses quaternion trackball camera controls, allowing continuous rotation

Interactive sketch SVG fills, edges, handles and annotations forward right/middle

## Unified sketch dimensions and sketch navigation controls — 2026-09-13

D and the ribbon Dimension button now enter one canvas authoring tool. The ribbon
no longer asks users to choose a dimension type. Select a line, circle, arc, two
points or two lines, move the live annotation, then click to place it. Geometry
and placement infer length, diameter, radius, aligned/H/V distance, parallel-line
spacing or angle. A compact unit-aware input with confirm/cancel applies the
existing solver operation; pending previews add no constraint. Confirmation keeps
the tool ready for the next measurement, Escape cancels, and keyboard shortcuts
leave typing, IME composition and modifiers alone. Existing driving annotations
open the same editor; their pending input survives repeated selection and unit
changes. Numeric expressions, undo/redo and native save/reopen use existing APIs.
Dimension labels retain their SVG size instead of the old global 11px CSS override;
measurement lines have arrowheads and selected geometry highlights during editing.
This does not add spline-length or ellipse-axis solver semantics.

Sketch selection now supports screen-space window/crossing drags, multiple edges,
curves and vertices, modifier-add selection, multiple-contour copy and selected
references as input to Dimension. Edge geometry is sampled for crossing tests;
a rectangle entirely inside a circle selects its center, not its circumference.
Flat and oblique world-mounted sketches use the same selection logic, with a
viewer projection bridge. Drag boxes are transient and commit selection on release. Pointer capture and
cancellation prevent stuck gestures when released outside the viewport.
Existing entity dragging and dimension-label dragging retain their own hit targets.
Space now opens the origin-centered navigation cube during sketch editing; cube
picking takes priority over sketch input, and framing includes active sketch bounds.
Text fields retain Space as text.

## Sketch drag placement and temporary alignment guides — 2026-09-13

Selection dragging hides closed-region shading while retaining sketch edges and
handles. Fill returns on release/cancel. Dragging uses a real point on the selected
entity and preserves the cursor's grab offset, instead of snapping the cursor to
its own moving geometry. Stable endpoints, circle/arc centers, midpoints,
construction geometry and the origin provide snap targets; stationary points in
the same contour also provide horizontal/vertical alignment. Geometry that follows
the drag through constraints is excluded from target acquisition.

Dashed guides and target rings exist only during an acquired snap. Moving past the
pixel-scaled tolerance clears the inference, and Alt bypasses snapping. Preview
uses existing Core drag solving without adding saved constraints; release evaluates
the final pointer position and commits geometry plus supported coincident,
concentric, midpoint, origin-fix or point-pair H/V relationships in one undo step.
Axis guides to computed centers/midpoints or origin remain positioning aids when
there is no existing point-pair relation to persist; no helper construction geometry
is silently added. Existing constraints take precedence over conflicting inference.
Escape, cancellation and lost capture restore the pre-drag geometry and shading.

Verified: CAD715 tests passed (three opt-in skips); typecheck/theme guard/build pass.
Nine focused drag tests cover acquire/release, final pointer coordinates, commit-only
inference, live target motion, same-contour alignment, concentric rings, midpoint,
Alt and blocked geometry. The existing free-drag undo test now explicitly uses Alt.
Approved isolated browser verified actual pointer drag: fill none + horizontal guide,
breakout clears guide, release restores gray fill. Native saved QA document contains

## Recoverable missing feature references — 2026-09-13

Deleting a Part feature now removes only the selected feature. Dependent sketches,
solids and construction planes remain editable in the Feature tree with red Error
rows, an error badge and a reference explanation on the icon. Missing references
survive native save/reopen as recoverable definitions; malformed values and forward
references still fail structural validation. Failed geometry and dependent sketch
curves, region picks and planes are excluded from the viewport. Unrelated valid
bodies remain, and Undo/restoring a source rebuilds the dependents and clears errors.

The normal edit/rebuild path and explicit FreeCAD Build command share recovery:
known per-feature native/translation failures propagate through the dependency
graph, then a fresh native document rebuilds the valid remainder. Geometry returned
by a failed native attempt is discarded. Runtime failures never overwrite persisted
Suppress flags. Transport/protocol failures still reject the operation. Legacy
implicit body targets are pinned before deletion so operations cannot switch bodies;
dependencies follow each preceding body modification, sketch support, selected
profile/path and construction-plane references.

checks; seven recovery tests with native FreeCAD enabled, covering missing support,
deleted source, zero-body result, independent bodies and restoration. Full CAD run:

## View leaves the ribbon; Design gets its five tabs back — 2026-09-13

The top bar is for modelling, so the View tray no longer has a ribbon tab. Its
six groups — Orientation, Display, Scene, Material, Ground, Panels — are right
sidebar panels, below a divider under the existing panel switches. Opening
Orientation gives Fit Model, Top, Bottom, Front, Back, Right, Left, Isometric
and Save View as a list, and the tool the viewport is currently in is marked, so
Display shows which shading mode is live.

They were flyout menus on the rail first, which was wrong twice over: a portal
menu has none of the panel window's chrome, and it floated over whatever panel
was already open beside it. As panels they inherit both — the same card, and the
shell's one-panel-per-side rule, so opening Orientation closes Properties
instead of covering it. `WorkspacePanel` gained `separatorBefore` to keep the
divider; the `railExtras` slot that carried the flyouts is gone, and so is the
floating strip that carried them before that.

Each panel reads its group from `cadRibbonWorkspace("view")`, so the panels and
the ribbon can never disagree about what a View tool is.

A docked toolbar now spans the window, with the sidebars under it, rather than
sitting in the column between them. It was the first child of `.aui-shell-main`,
inside `.aui-shell-area` and so between the two `.aui-shell-side` columns; it is
now the first child of `.aui-shell-body`, above that area. Measured at 1700px
wide: the toolbar runs 0 to 1700 and both sides start below it. This is
`WorkspaceShell`, so Aether Animation's docked preset gets the same shape.

The ribbon overflows that full width on the Solid tab, and could not be
scrolled with a mouse: `.cad-ribbon-scroll` has always been `overflow-x: auto`,
but a wheel reports only `deltaY`, so nothing moved, and macOS hides overlay
scrollbars until they move, so the row simply looked cut off. A wheel with no
horizontal component now moves the ribbon sideways — `ribbonScrollStep` returns
0 when the ribbon fits, and 0 when the gesture already carries `deltaX`, so a
trackpad swipe is still the browser's to handle — and the scrollbar is a slim
persistent 7px bar rather than an overlay.

Their rail buttons came out at twice the size of the panel switches beside them:
`AetherIcon` sizes itself in `em` and landed at 17px, while `ToolIcon` carries
its own 32px and filled the whole 32px button. A rail button's icon is now 1em
whichever component drew it, so both measure 17.

The Design workspace shows Fusion's tabs again: Solid, Surface, Mesh, Sheet
Metal, Plastic, then Manage and Output. Those five were removed on 2026-09-12
because they were a second hand-written taxonomy that re-listed Solid's tool ids
and drifted from the traditional ribbon. They are back as catalog trays, so both
ribbon presentations render the same tabs from one definition. Surface, Mesh,
Sheet Metal and Plastic are entirely greyed and each says which half is missing:
a translation Aether has not written, a body type it does not have, a FreeCAD
add-on it does not ship, or a feature FreeCAD has no workbench for. Solid is the
only one of the five whose tools mostly run.

The suite ribbon's active tab was painting `--aether-color-accent-icon` text on
`--aether-color-bg-selected`: measured rgb(47,127,224) on rgb(50,115,214), an
unreadable blue-on-blue. It uses `--aether-color-text-on-selected`, the token
that pairs with that background.


The ribbon had two Sketch tabs: a permanent one and the contextual one that
opens while a sketch is being edited. The permanent tab is gone — its tools
only apply inside a sketch — and Solid > Modeling opens with Create Sketch, as
Fusion's Create list does. The contextual tab no longer offers Create Sketch
either: nobody draws a sketch inside a sketch, so its Create group starts at
Point.

Home is the document tray now: Project and Selection, nothing else. Its Create
and Modify groups were Sketch, Rebuild Extrude, Cut, Revolve, Fillet, Chamfer
and Shell — seven tools that already sit on Solid and run the same commands.

Assembly is a workspace, not a file prompt. Picking it in the switcher used to
run Open Assembly and put a file dialog up; it now changes `workspaceMode` and
shows the assembly ribbon over the same live 3D viewport, the way Design does.
`CADWorkspaceMode` gained an `"assembly"` member for it, and only Drawing makes
the viewport inert now.

Its tabs are Onshape's: **Build, Mates, Relations, Inspect**, plus Manage and
Output — no Solid, Surface, Mesh, Sheet Metal, Framing or Plastic, because an
assembly does none of that work. The one Assembly tray split into four, one file
each. Build brings parts in (New/Open/Save Assembly, Insert Part, Smart Fastener,

Relations holds the driven-motion joints; Inspect holds review and measurement.
The Assembly workspace also gets the Fusion-style presentation, which was
part-only.

An open assembly resets `workspaceMode` to `"modeling"`, so the switcher reads
its label from the effective workspace — an open assembly is the Assembly
workspace however you reached it.

New Part and New Assembly left the Design ribbon: creating a document is not a
modelling operation. The workspace switcher beside the tabs, which had been an
inert menu with `onSelect={() => {}}`, is now real — Design, Assembly and
Drawing switch workspaces, and the button names the one you are in. New Part
moved to Home > Project beside Open Part; New Assembly was already in the
Assembly tray's Structure group.

`fusionTabsFor` read the raw catalog trays rather than the resolved workspace,
so the layout's `excludeTools` applied to the traditional ribbon and not to the
Fusion one. That is why a Part document's Home tab showed New Assembly and the
Component selection filter. Both presentations now render
`toolbarWorkspaceFor`, and a test compares the two.

Framing is a tab of its own — Frame, Frame trim, Gusset, End cap, Cut list, all

greyed Frame is gone; Framing owns framing.

Sheet Metal carries Onshape's list in its order — Sheet metal model, Flange,

Corner break, Finish sheet metal model, Flex PCB model, Finish flex PCB model.
All fifteen are greyed against the same reason: no SheetMetal add-on, and no

existing docked behavior.

## Sketch constraint relationship markers — 2026-09-13

Committed sketch relationships use 13 centered monochrome SVG symbols from
`core/assets/icons/relationships/`, replacing font glyphs in their badges.
Leader lines connect badges to their participants. Multi-entity relationships
show matching badges at distinct anchors; colocated anchors merge. Placement
avoids other badges, sampled geometry and vertices/centers, preferring nearby
free positions rather than long stacks.

In Select mode, hovering a badge highlights the relationship's actual points,
edges, curves/circles and symmetry axis in gold. Related badges highlight together.
Keyboard focus also exposes the participants; hover/blur and Show constraints
cleanup remove transient highlighting. Hit-testing handles events forwarded by
the 3D viewer and prevents marker clicks from placing points or dragging geometry.
Drawing and modification tools retain their own gestures.

`relationships/interaction.ts` is a generic presentation adapter with typed
participants; `sketch/constraint-geometry.ts` projects existing Core references,
including stable/projected edges, without adding another model or solver.
Assembly mates and plane/support views have not been migrated to these markers.
Broken references are not guessed. This packet covers the 13 catalog relationship
kinds; dimensions retain their separate annotations.

Jonathan's “ok do it” packet is implemented. This entry supersedes the earlier

- New Extrude features allow several selected contours, using stable IDs. Native

- Part ribbon Inspect now exposes Section and Interference. Sections use native

# STATUS

> Truthful, or it's worthless. Any commit that changes behavior updates
> this file in the same commit — see `CONVENTIONS.md` → "STATUS stays
> truthful."

## Complete rendered faces on native solids — 2026-09-12

Fixed the FreeCAD display adapter's face-range units. Native `face_ranges`
counts triangles; Three.js material groups and viewport picking use index-buffer
entries. Passing the counts unchanged drew only one third of the indices,
making a solid circle extrusion look like an incomplete thin wall. The adapter
now converts both start and count by ×3. No native geometry or saved features
needed changing.

Reproduction: native radius 10 mm/depth 20 mm cylinder had three faces,
6283.185307 mm³ and 1500 indices, but its display groups covered only 500.
Regression checks now cover all 1500 indices exactly once and map every
triangle to the correct wall/cap for picking. Focused adapter/picking/client
tests passed (16); production build passed. Browser acceptance loaded a circle
Part through the actual native build/committed viewport path and showed a
complete capped cylinder. Production assets are updated; QA data was isolated.

## Live solid-feature previews and explicit region selection — 2026-09-12

Available solid editors (Extrude, Revolve, Sweep, Shell, Fillet, Chamfer and
Mirror) now request a live native preview through the same candidate-document
builder and FreeCAD evaluator used by Apply. Region, dimension, operation and
target changes debounce for 180 ms; one in-flight request plus the latest pending
candidate avoids flooding the worker. Obsolete and closed-dialog replies cannot
restore old previews. A separate shaded viewport layer with orange edges shows
the resulting part without changing feature history, selection topology or saved
documents. Cancel restores committed geometry; Apply rebuilds the same candidate.
Native preview failures clear the temporary geometry, show the error and disable
Apply until corrected. This is not a promise of instantaneous server evaluation.

Profile chips now say e.g. `Sketch 1 · Region 4 · circle`. The dialog explicitly
states how many closed regions are selected and that only that region is used.
The viewport highlights the chosen contour, including when initialized from an
existing feature. Choosing a sketch is context for choosing a region; this does
not add whole-sketch/multiple-region extrusion or regions with holes.

Verification: full CAD suite 592 passed at the first preview checkpoint; final
focused suite 24 passed after error gating was added. Production build passed.
Browser acceptance on isolated data: a 19 mm extrusion previewed at 30 mm with
unchanged saved revision; Cancel restored the original. An invalid 1000 mm fillet
showed its native error with Apply disabled; correcting to 0.5 mm restored the
preview and enabled Apply without saving. DOM acceptance compares the preview
candidate with the submitted document; queue tests cover stale replies, cancel,
coalescing and error recovery. Normal production assets are rebuilt. No backend
restart or production-document edits were needed.

This establishes native solid previews, not full Onshape interaction parity:
on-canvas depth handles, preview opacity controls, whole-sketch/multi-region
operations and broader feature options remain unfinished.

## The ribbon condenses, and the menu lines up — 2026-09-13

- **The variant menu opened off the tool it belonged to.** `MenuButton`
  anchored to its own trigger, and on a ribbon tool the trigger is the caret —
  a small button to the right of the icon — so the menu started halfway across
  the tool. `MenuButton` now takes `anchorTo="group"`, which anchors to the
  element containing the trigger. Measured in the browser: the Circle menu's
  left edge is now exactly the tool's left edge, offset 0px.
- **The buttons were as wide as their longest label.** `min-width` was not
  what set the pitch — the label was, so tools ran 62px to 113px and the row
  looked loose. Two fixes: the label is wrapped in a span so it can be clipped
  rather than widen the button (the full text is already in the tooltip), and
  the primary labels are the *tool's* name rather than a variant's. A button
  saying "Inscribed polygon" was the variant's name doing the tool's job.
  Twenty-four labels shortened: Create Sketch -> Sketch, 3 point arc -> Arc,
  Cubic Bézier -> Spline, Inscribed polygon -> Polygon, and so on. The menu
  still names each kind in full.
- Ribbon spacing: section padding 10px -> 5px, tool gap 2px -> 0, caret
  18px -> 11px, tool padding 6px -> 2px. Every tool is now 62px, not 62-113px.
- The variant dropdown was sized like a dialog: min-width 190px -> 150px, rows
  36px -> 28px, icons 28px -> 22px. A three-item variant list is 158x96.
- One test had to change for the right reason: `getByText("Fastened")` used to
  return the button's text node and now returns the label span, so it asserted
  focus on the wrong element. It queries by role now, which is what it meant.
- Verification: 692 Aether CAD tests, 173 core/ui tests, typecheck and builds
  clean, and the result measured and screenshotted in a real browser.

## One catalog, two presentations — 2026-09-13

Jonathan's rule: every toolbar presentation shows the same tools, in the same
order, in the same groups; only the design differs. It did not.

- **The Part ribbon was a second taxonomy.** `PART_FUSION_TABS` was a
  hand-written arrangement — Solid, Surface, Mesh, Sheet Metal, Plastic,
  Manage, Utilities — that re-listed tool ids by hand. Measured against the
  catalog it named **69 of 205 tools**. A Part document could not reach:
  - every **View** command — 39 of them, the whole tab
  - 13 of the 21 **Home** tools
  - **FreeCAD Build**, the button that runs the default engine
  and it listed some tools twice across tabs (Loft and Sweep in both Solid and
  Surface).
- **It is now derived.** `fusionTabFor(workspace)` turns any catalog workspace
  into Fusion-style sections, and the Part tabs are simply the layout's tabs
  mapped through it. The presentation difference is the only difference: a few
  buttons plus an overflow menu, instead of a flat group.
- `sketchContextTab()` was already doing this for one workspace; it is now the
  same function.
- The hand-written taxonomy and its `section()` builder are gone —
  `cad-toolbar-layouts.ts` is 151 lines.
- **Guarded:** a test asserts the Fusion arrangement exposes exactly the tools
  the traditional ribbon does, in the same order, variants included. Drift
  cannot come back quietly.
- One bug worth naming: `tabs.map(fusionTabFor)` passed the array index as the
  second argument, which the function took as the tab id — tabs came out
  numbered 0-5. An explicit arrow fixes it, and the parity test caught it.
- Verification: 682 Aether CAD tests, typecheck and build clean.

## Tool variants reach the ribbon a Part actually shows — 2026-09-13

The sketch tools have carried `variants` in the catalog for some time, and the
*traditional* ribbon rendered the caret. A Part document does not use that
ribbon — it uses the Fusion layout — and that path's `renderTool` drew a bare
button. So Line, Rectangle, Arc, Circle and Polygon looked flat and their
variants were unreachable, which is why this read as never implemented.

- **`renderTool` in the Fusion path now renders the caret**, shares the same
  selected-variant state as the traditional ribbon, and keeps the button on
  the last kind picked — Onshape's behaviour.
- **The section overflow lists variants.** Onshape's `Create` menu shows every
  drawing tool including the ones behind carets; ours listed only the top-level
  entries.
- **Eight tools show as buttons, not six.** Circle and Inscribed polygon were
  past the cut and reachable only through the overflow.
- **The 3D tools are grouped the same way now**: Extrude carries Revolve,
  Sweep and Loft; Fillet carries Chamfer, Variable and Face fillet; Move
  carries Copy, Rotate and Scale. Their flat duplicates in Advanced Shape and
  Transform are gone — a tool is listed once, and the catalog's uniqueness
  test enforces it.
- Two tests had to learn about variants: the catalog's coverage check counted
  only top-level tools, so grouping Loft under Extrude read as Loft having
  been deleted.
- Thirteen grouped buttons in total. Verification: 680 Aether CAD tests,
  typecheck and build clean.
- **Missing and not added: Conic.** It is in Onshape's arc dropdown and we have
  no equivalent. It is not a toolbar entry — it needs a sketch primitive with
  solver and geometry support — so it belongs in the sketch engine, not here.

## References are named, not described — 2026-09-13

The sketch plane chip read `Body 1 · planar face · attached` — a sentence
about the chip. Onshape shows `Plane 1`, `Face of Extrude 1`: the thing you
picked. A reference is an identity, and describing it tells a reader nothing
about which one it is.

| Picked | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Principal plane | `XY plane` | `Top Plane` / `Front Plane` / `Right Plane` |
| Datum plane | `Selected plane` | `Plane 1` — its own name |
| Planar face | `Body 1 · planar face · attached` | `Face of Extrude 1` |
| Face in the viewport | `Body 1 · Face -1154006771` | `Face 3 of Body 1` |

- `supportForFace` already resolved the feature that made the face; it now
  names it instead of rewriting the label into "planar face".
- **Face ids are hashes**, not numbers a reader can use. They stay the
  identity a saved reference resolves against, but the ordinal is what is
  shown — the same thing FreeCAD and Onshape display.
- The principal names match the reference-geometry tree, so the chip and the
  tree call the same plane the same thing.
- `· attached` is gone. It described the chip's state rather than saying which
  face it pointed at.
- Verification: 670 Aether CAD tests, including DOM tests that click each
  plane kind and assert the chip text, and one asserting the old wording is
  absent. Typecheck and build clean.

## The assembly path joins up — 2026-09-13

The gap named yesterday is closed: the UI now solves through FreeCAD.

- **`assembly-job.ts`** turns the open assembly document into a job. Metres to
  millimetres — the projection is in metres because it is shared with the
  animation engine's rig semantics, and every length the CAD engine takes is
  millimetres, which is exactly where this would have drifted silently.
  Suppressed instances and mates are left out, sub-assemblies are reported as
  not solved yet, and a part with no feature document is named rather than
  quietly dropped.
- **A mate connector is a joint coordinate system.** `JointEnd` now carries a
  frame, and the engine sets FreeCAD's `Placement1`/`Placement2` with
  `Detach`, so the connector is used verbatim instead of being recomputed from
  geometry. Proved: a mate between connectors offset from their part origins
  lands the block at (30, 30, 10), not (0, 0, 0). Live over HTTP, three
  instances and two mate kinds solved in 102 ms.
- **`startup/assembly-solve.ts`** places the solved bodies. Parts are built
  through the same evaluator a Part document uses, and each body is named by
  its instance so two of the same part are tellable apart.
- **The ribbon needs both halves, and I nearly shipped it needing one.**
  FreeCAD solves thirteen kinds, so the Assembly tab offered thirteen. But a
  mate is still committed through the workspace's `add_mate`, which takes the
  three of Assembly v1 — clicking Ball would have failed *after* the user had
  authored the whole mate. Three are enabled; fourteen are greyed with two
  distinct reasons: ten say FreeCAD solves it but Assembly v1 cannot author it
  yet, four say FreeCAD has no joint for it at all.
  `test_cad_mate_capability_contract.py` now guards the ribbon too, and fails
  naming the offending kind.
- Each mate kind is its own button and the dialog opens on that kind — the
  event it dispatches is consumed, checked rather than assumed after the first
  version of it went nowhere.
- Verification: 660 Aether CAD tests, 1329 Python tests, ruff, typecheck and
  builds clean; the app driven in a browser with no page errors.
- **Still not done:** Anima Studio archival.

## Assemblies on the FreeCAD engine — 2026-09-12

Jonathan's call after the mate investigation: use FreeCAD's own assembly
solver. The engine, the protocol, the host endpoints and the ribbon are in;
the last link — mapping an open assembly document into a job — is not.

**Engine.** `aether_freecad/assembly.py` drives FreeCAD's
`Assembly::AssemblyObject` and the Ondsel multibody solver, headless.
Stateless like the geometry path: an `AssemblyJob` carries its own part
definitions, so the engine holds no document between calls and the same job
always solves to the same placements. A part is built through
`_apply_feature` — extracted from `_build` for this — so a part behaves
identically whether it is opened alone or placed in an assembly.

**Vocabulary.** Aether's mate names (`fastened`, `prismatic`) live in
`protocol.py` and are translated to FreeCAD's (`Fixed`, `Slider`) inside the
worker, so saved assemblies never carry FreeCAD's names and the engine stays
replaceable — the same rule face identity follows. Thirteen kinds.

**Nothing is grounded** is a warning, not a silent answer: with nothing fixed
the whole assembly is free to drift and any solution is as good as any other,
so the first instance is held and the diagnostic says so.

**Host.** `/api/cad/assembly` solves; `/api/cad/mate-kinds` reports what the
engine can actually build, so the ribbon asks rather than assumes — the lesson
from Shell and Sweep, where it would be worse here because a refusal would
land only after the user had authored the whole mate.

**Ribbon.** The Assembly tab is rebuilt around mates: twelve enabled
(Fastened, Revolute, Slider, Cylindrical, Ball, Distance, Parallel,
Perpendicular, Angle, Gears, Rack and Pinion, Screw, Belt) and four greyed
with a reason — Planar, Pin Slot, Tangent and Width are Onshape mates FreeCAD
has no joint for. Existing tool ids were kept; only the command each runs
changed. Each kind is its own button rather than a generic Mate that then
asks which.

**Icons.** Five new mate icons — ball, cylindrical, gears, belt, rack-pinion —
drawn in the existing 32px tool style (themed gradients, `--tool-*` variables,
orange dashed axes) and registered in `@aether/ui`.

**Verified:** 8 new engine tests including a fastened mate moving a block from
(120, 75, 33) onto its target and a distance mate holding parts exactly 25mm
apart — a mate the previous engine did not have. Live over HTTP: solved in
0.24s. 634 Aether CAD tests, 163 core/ui tests, 116 Python tests, ruff,
typecheck and builds clean.

**Not done, and not pretended:** `solveAssembly()` is written and tested at
the engine and HTTP level but nothing in the UI calls it yet — the ribbon's
Solve still re-solves through the existing aether_animation path. Mapping an open
assembly document into an `AssemblyJob` is the next packet. The Assembly tab
is also not reachable while a Part document is open, because the Part layout
excludes it; that predates this work. Anima Studio archival has not started.

## Where mates actually live, and a guard on the CAD slice — 2026-09-12

Answering a direct question with evidence rather than assumption.

- **Correction: FreeCAD does have mates.** *Our binding* has none — a grep
  for "mate" across `aether_freecad/` finds only comments — but FreeCAD
  1.1.3 ships an Assembly workbench with the Ondsel multibody solver and
  thirteen joint types, and it runs headless. Verified in `freecadcmd`:
  `AssemblyObject.solve()` converged
  `33665571 -> 3176 -> 76 -> 0.087 -> 4.8e-08 -> 0` and moved a block from
  `(120, 75, 33)` to `(0, 0, 0)` through a Fixed joint. That reopens where
  CAD mates should be solved — see
  `dev/docs/roadmap/Mates_Engine_Decision.md`.
- **Mates are aether_animation.** `aether_animation/mates.py` (674 lines) and
  `kinematics.py` (577) own the ten typed mates and solve them; the CAD app
  reaches them over `/{app}/rpc`, which the host proxies to
  `aether_animation.bridge`. They are live, not future work: `test_mates.py` covers
  every kind's schema, `test_bridge_aether_workspace.py` (746 lines) exercises
  `add_mate`, `solve_assembly` and `set_dof_value`, and a call to `/cad/rpc`
  against the running host answers.
- **CAD exposes three of the ten.** `aether_workspace` advertises
  `supported_mate_type_ids` as fastened / revolute / prismatic and refuses the
  rest with `unsupported_capability` — the deliberate Assembly v1 slice. The
  other seven (parallel, cylindrical, pin-slot, planar, ball, width, tangent)
  exist in the engine and serve the animation product.
- **New guard:** `test_cad_mate_capability_contract.py`. The CAD dialog builds
  its Type dropdown from a hand-written list in `cad-mate-authoring.ts` while
  the workspace advertises its own. The two agreed by coincidence, not by
  construction — the same shape as the bug that shipped Shell and Sweep, but
  worse here, because the user would author a mate and have the commit refused
  afterwards. The test reads both as text, so it needs no Node and no build,
  and it fails when they drift.
- **Not done, deliberately: one file per mate type.** The design is
  table-driven — `JOINT_TYPE_DOF_TEMPLATES` gives each of the ten kinds its DOF
  tuple and every function is parameterised by `JointType`. Per-type branching
  across the whole engine is one line in `kinematics.py` and a handful in
  `loader.py`. Ten files would each hold a one-to-six line tuple, plus a
  registry to reassemble what is currently a thirty-line table you can read at
  a glance. `tools/` and `features/` were worth splitting because each item
  carried 40-145 lines of its own behaviour; a mate carries data.

## Shell and Sweep build, and the lane gap has a guard — 2026-09-12

- **Shell and Sweep were enabled with nothing behind them.** The same shape as
  `sketch-wire`: the toolbar un-greyed them, `freecad-translate.ts` emitted
  `shell` and `sweep`, and `worker.py` had no builder, so clicking either
  would have failed at build time. Sweep now builds as PartDesign
  `AdditivePipe`/`SubtractivePipe`; shell as `PartDesign::Thickness`, choosing
  the faces it opens by the plane they lie in — the same rule edge finishes
  use, so a saved part never depends on FreeCAD's face numbering. A shell
  whose opening plane matches no face is refused rather than silently shelling
  the solid closed.
- **A cross-lane guard, because this was the third time.**
  `tests/test_translation_contract.py` reads the kinds `freecad-translate.ts`
  emits and the kinds `worker.py` dispatches, and fails when the translator
  can produce something the engine cannot build. It parses both as text, so it
  needs no Node, no build and no FreeCAD, and a second test pins known kinds so
  a regex that silently matched nothing cannot make it pass forever. Verified
  by removing the sweep branch: it fails and names the kind.
- **Audit of the ribbon, for the record.** 203 tools, every one defined exactly
  once in `cad-tool-catalog.ts`; 128 carry an action, 75 are greyed and every
  greyed one carries a reason the UI shows. `cad-toolbar-layouts.ts` holds two
  *arrangements* (the Home/Sketch/3D Tools tabs and the Fusion-style Part
  tabs) that reference tools by id only — it defines none, and no id it names
  is missing from the catalog. All eight feature tools (plane, extrude,
  revolve, mirror, fillet, chamfer, shell, sweep) are now backed end to end:
  editor, translation and worker builder.
- Verification: 23 FreeCAD engine tests, 75 Python tests, 558 Aether CAD
  tests, ruff, typecheck and build clean.

## `sketch-wire` builds, and an open profile stops vanishing — 2026-09-12

- **`unsupported feature kind 'sketch-wire'`.** The translator gained a
  `sketch-wire` kind for drawn contours that are not plain polygons or
  circles; the FreeCAD worker had no builder for it, so any part holding a
  curved region failed to build. `_wire_sketch` now builds line, arc and
  cubic-bezier segments. Sketcher takes a `Part.Arc` as-is but rejects a raw
  `Part.BezierCurve` ("Unsupported geometry type: Part::GeomBezierCurve"), so
  a bezier goes in as the degree-3 B-spline it already is, via `toBSpline()`.
  Consecutive pieces are joined with coincidence constraints, and a contour
  whose end meets its start is closed.
- **An open profile built nothing and said nothing.** FreeCAD pads an open
  wire to no solid and still reports success, so the feature simply left the
  part with no diagnostic. Pad, pocket and revolve now check the profile has
  a closed wire and refuse with a reason. This is the failure a hand-drawn
  region is most likely to hit.
- **The ribbon switching tab sets is not duplication.** There is one catalog
  (`cadRibbonWorkspaces`) and one component. `CADTraditionalRibbon` renders
  Fusion-style tabs when `fusionTabsFor(documentType)` returns them — which
  is only for `"part"` — and the Home/Sketch/3D Tools set otherwise.
  `documentType` is `"part"` only while `activePartDocument !== null`, so a
  part that fails to open falls back to the project layout and the whole tab
  set appears to change. The toolbar was reporting the load failure, not
  causing it. Worth deciding whether a failed load should really restyle the
  ribbon.
- Verification: 18 FreeCAD engine tests (2 new: a curved wire pads to a
  5-faced solid; an open one is refused by name), 70 Python tests, 557 Aether
  CAD tests, ruff, typecheck and build clean, and the curved wire confirmed
  through the running host.

## Sketch regions are pickable, and the sketch gets out of the way — 2026-09-12

- **The shaded interiors are now selectable.** `pickSketchRegion` in
  `sketch/picking.ts` hit-tests a click against closed contours by
  containment, not proximity — edges and vertices are picked by being *near*,
  a region by being *in*. Curves are flattened with the existing
  `sketchContourPolyline`, so circles and arcs work, not just straight runs.
  The smallest containing region wins, so a shape drawn inside another is
  still reachable. Construction and open contours bound nothing and are
  skipped.
- **Reaching for a solid tool commits the sketch.** Clicking Extrude (or any
  solid feature) while the sketch editor is open now fires the previously
  unused `aether-sketch-finish`, waits for the editor to go, and opens the
  feature on the document the sketch just produced — instead of stacking two
  windows. A sketch that refuses to commit keeps its own error visible and no
  feature dialog opens over it.
- **The region carries across.** `sketch-region-selection.ts` is a one-shot
  channel: the sketch editor puts the picked region in, the next feature
  dialog takes it out, which clears it — so a later Extrude cannot inherit a
  stale pick.
- **The plane stopped shouting.** Sketch plane fill .09 -> .03, its outline
  .8 -> .28, grid .3 -> .14, title .85 -> .45; contours went to 2.1px and a
  brighter stroke, closed regions from `2a` to `33` alpha. The sheet is
  context; the profile is the content.
- Not built: a live preview of the feature being authored, and this session
  did not verify viewport-side region picking — another agent is building
  that concurrently on the `aether-region-mode` / `aether-region-picked`
  events in `features/regions.ts`.
- Verification: 556 Aether CAD tests (5 new for region hit-testing),
  typecheck and build clean. The sketch-to-feature auto-close is wired but

## Extruding one region of a multi-region sketch — 2026-09-12

Jonathan drew one sketch holding four separate closed shapes, tried to pick one
and extrude it, and could not. Nothing was broken: the capability had never
been built, in three places at once.

- **A sketch with more than one contour did not translate at all.**
  `polygonFromStraightContour` opened with `if (contours.length !== 1) return
  null`, so any drawn sketch holding several regions was refused whole — not
  just per-region extrude, but *any* build from that sketch. Each closed,
  non-construction contour now becomes its own engine sketch
  (`s1#0`, `s1#1`, …), and circles translate as well as straight runs. A sketch
  holding one region keeps the plain feature id, so saved documents translate
  exactly as before.
- **`ExtrudeFeature` had no way to name a region.** It carried only
  `profileFeatureId` — the whole sketch. It now takes an optional
  `profileContourId`, the contour's own stable id scoped to its source profile,
  so reordering or editing coordinates cannot retarget the extrude. Revolve
  resolves regions through the same path.
- **The dialog offered no choice.** The Extrude window's "Faces and sketch
  regions to extrude" was a plain `<select>` of whole sketches. It now has a
  Region picker, populated from the same `sketchRegions()` list the translator
  uses, so picker and engine can never disagree about what a region is or what
  order they come in. The row hides itself when the chosen sketch holds only
  one region. Identity is stamped on the contour only when it is actually
  picked, on the document being committed — the rule
  `referenceProfileContour` already follows.
- **Ambiguity is refused, not guessed.** Several regions with none chosen
  disables the accept control and says how many there are; a named region that
  has since left the sketch is reported rather than silently rebuilt as
  something else.
- Still not built: picking a region by clicking it in the 3D viewport. The
  choice is made in the Extrude dialog. Arcs and splines in a drawn contour
  still do not translate, and now say which region they blocked.
- Verification: 540 Aether CAD tests (9 new, covering the multi-region
  translation, the picker, and the refusals), 737 engine tests, build and
  typecheck clean. Against real FreeCAD, the translator's own output for a
  three-region sketch padded only the named circle: 301.593mm³, exactly
  pi*4^2*6. Driven in a browser against the running host, the Extrude dialog
  opens with the Region row and no page errors.

## FreeCAD face identity corrected, and four more features translated — 2026-09-12

- **Correction to the entry below: `hashCode` did not give stable face IDs.**
  `Part.Face.hashCode()` is the address of the underlying OCCT `TShape`, so it
  is a fresh number on every build. Measured against the running host: the same
  job posted twice returned six entirely different `faceId` values. A
  construction plane saves the id of the face it was built on
  (`construction-planes.ts` → `{ kind: "face"; faceId }`), so that id must
  survive a rebuild. Face ids are now derived from geometry — surface kind,
  centre of mass and area, hashed with blake2b to a signed 32-bit int, with an
  occurrence counter separating coincident faces. Tessellation and topology
  take their ids from one shared `stable_face_ids(shape)` so a triangle's
  `faceId` is the id its topology entry is filed under. Verified: the same job
  built in two separate FreeCAD processes returns identical ids.
  **Known limit:** ids are deterministic, not invariant under edits — a face
  whose geometry moves gets a new id. Provenance-tracking naming through the
  feature history is still open work.
- **Every face frame was a broken frame.** `FreeCAD.Vector.multiply()` scales
  the receiver in place and returns it; `_connector_axes` did
  `x_axis_fallback.sub(z.multiply(dot))`, which scaled the very normal it was
  about to return. For any face square to the fallback X axis — four of a box's
  six — `dot` was 0 and the normal came back as the zero vector. Snaps, mates
  and sketch-on-face all hang off these frames. Three in-place mutations fixed
  (a third compounded across cylinder axis stations inside a loop). A box now
  reports six unit, mutually square frames.
- **Revolve, mirror, fillet and chamfer now reach FreeCAD.** The document
  already modelled them and the toolbar already offered Revolve, Fillet,
  Chamfer and Mirror; nothing translated them, so they silently landed in
  `untranslated` and built nothing. `freecad-translate.ts` now maps them and
  `worker.py` builds them as PartDesign Revolution/Groove, Mirrored, Fillet and
  Chamfer. Edge finishes select edges by the plane they lie in, matching the
  TypeScript engine, so a saved part does not depend on FreeCAD's edge
  numbering. Revolve volumes check against Pappus' theorem. A mirror that cuts
  is still reported untranslated rather than silently added.
- **`npm run dev` could not reach the backend at all.** The dev server
  proxied only `/rpc`, and the host derives the origin it expects from the
  `Host` header, so even with a proxy entry a POST was refused. `/api` now
  proxies with `changeOrigin` and a matching `Origin`.
- Verification: 16 FreeCAD engine tests (up from 6, one of which was failing),
  531 Aether CAD tests, 52 host tests, 1203 aether_animation tests, `ruff` clean,
  typecheck and production build clean. The app was driven in a real browser
  against the running host: the editor opens, renders and calls
  `/api/cad/geometry` with no page errors.

## FreeCAD Stable Topological Naming — 2026-09-12

- **FreeCAD Topological Naming Solved at the Boundary.** The exact-topology stable identity system from the parked `@aether/core` TypeScript engine has been successfully ported into the `aether_freecad` Python engine. `worker.py` now exports stable face IDs using OCCT's `hashCode` via FreeCAD's Python API instead of generating sequential arrays (`Face1`, `Face2`).
- **Mating Candidates in Python.** The Python worker now natively extracts analytical `CenterOfMass`, axes, and exact `ConnectorCandidate` metadata (face centers, edge midpoints, circle centers, etc.) from FreeCAD solids and serves them across the JSON boundary. FreeCAD acts as the geometry engine, but Aether dictates the stable parametric naming.

## FreeCAD Host Backend Wired to Frontend — 2026-09-12

- **FreeCAD powers Aether CAD via Host RPC.** Implemented Jonathan's engine decision by wiring the browser frontend to the `/api/cad/geometry` endpoint. The new `HostAetherCoreClient` sends `features` and `rollbackIndex` over JSON, removing the heavy parametric feature evaluation from the browser's parked `@aether/core` engine. The server (FreeCAD Python JSON backend) crunches the exact B-Rep solid math statelessly and responds with B-Rep topology ready for WebGPU.
- **WASM fallback for interactive tasks.** `HostAetherCoreClient` delegates `importSTEP` back to the existing embedded `OCCTWorkerClient` to maintain fast, local, native parsing in the browser, fulfilling the intended Onshape-style architecture of lightweight browser operations combined with heavy server geometry evaluation.
- Verification: typecheck and production build in `Aether CAD` passed cleanly.

## Product-owned CAD engine, and sketch-plane fixes — 2026-09-11

- **The CAD engine moved to `Aether CAD/engine/`.** It was `core/engine/`, named `@aether/core` as though suite-shared, but its only consumers were Aether CAD (104 files) and two `core/ui/gallery` demos — `aether-animation/web` never imported it. Aether Studio is the server (`core/host/`, `core/session/`); products own their engines, the way Onshape owns its kernel binding and feature library. Import name `@aether/core` is unchanged, so no consumer source changed; only dependency wiring and two asset paths that reached out of the package. `core/ui` now carries the engine as a **devDependency** for its gallery demos only, so the shared design system no longer sits downstream of one product's engine — `aether-animation/web/node_modules/@aether/` contains only `ui`. Verified: 462 CAD tests + typecheck + build, 719 engine tests, 163 core/ui tests + typecheck + build, animation web build.
- **Sketches render again, and the sketch plane is a real object.** The in-world sketch SVG is reparented into the viewer's CSS3D layer, but 40 geometry CSS rules were still scoped to the workspace ancestor, so every line drew with `stroke:none` — nothing appeared. The plane is now one 160 mm square anchored to the selected plane's (or planar face's) frame origin, with face, grid, axes, origin marker and name label all drawn inside it; it no longer follows the pan/zoom viewport. The world floor grid hides while a sketch is open, so a sketch on XY no longer shows a second, perpendicular grid beside it.
- **Reference-plane visibility persists** across reloads and is no longer discarded when a sketch finishes. **Placing a sketch plane no longer arms the line tool** — the first click selects until a tool is chosen.
- **The sketch feature window matches the Aether UI gallery again.** Nine bare-element rules under `.cad-sketch-workspace` outranked the shared widget's own styling and repainted it (the green accept and red discard had become neutral bordered boxes); every control the app creates there is `display:none`, so those rules styled nothing else. Also `index.html` pinned `color-scheme: dark`, painting native checkboxes as black squares inside light panels.

- Core `solver/point-line-measurement.ts` owns shared measurement geometry; solver residuals, reference measurement and CAD annotations consume it. Canvas extension lines terminate at the perpendicular foot, including beyond a segment endpoint. Distance relations are classified as preserving the supporting line for split remapping.

## Driving/reference dimension conversion — 2026-09-09
